notes.3: (tn, Heb): “in the days of” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*דבר.* 
המורשתי מעיר מורישה:
rashi.eng: *Micah the Morashtite.* From the city Mareshah.

notes.8: (tn, Heb): “O earth and all its fullness”; KJV “and all that therein is.”
notes.9: (tn, Heb): “May the sovereign Lord testify against you.” The verb וִיהִי (vihiy) is jussive, which normally conveys a volitional sense of an urgent request or prayer (“may he testify!”). However, GKC 325-26 �109.k notes that here the jussive form is used without any volitional sense for the ordinary imperfect, as a rhythmic shortening at the beginning of a sentence, thus removed as far as possible from the principal accent (cf. Gen 49:17; Deut 28:8; 1 Sam 10:5; 2 Sam 5:24; Hos 6:1; 11:4; Amos 5:14; Zeph 2:13; Zech 9:5; Pss 72:16-17; 104:31; Job 18:12; 20:23, 26, 28; 27:8; 33:21; 34:37; Ruth 3:4). Thus, the translation here renders the jussive as an ordinary imperfect. Some translations render it in a traditional jussive sense: (1) urgent request: “And let my Lord God be your accuser” (NJPS); or (2) dependent purpose/result: “that the Sovereign Lord may witness against you” (NIV).
notes.10: (tn, Heb): “the Lord from his majestic palace.” Since the verb is omitted it is unclear whether the implied term be supplied from the preceding line (“he will testify against you”) or the following line (“he is leaving”). So the line may be rendered “the Lord will accuse you from his majestic temple” or “the Lord will come forth from his majestic temple.” Most translations render it literally, but some remove the ambiguity: “the Lord God accuses you from his holy temple” (CEV); “He speaks from his holy temple” (TEV).
notes.11: (tn): Or “his holy temple” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). This refers to the Lord’s dwelling in heaven, however, rather than the temple in Jerusalem (note the following verse, which describes a theophany).

rashi.heb:
*ויהי, בכם לעד.* 
שנבאתי לכם בשמו והתריתי בכם:
rashi.eng: *and let the Lord be a witness against you.* that I prophesied to you in His Name and warned you.

notes.12: (tn): Or “For look.” The expression כִּי־הִנֵּה (ki-hinneh) may function as an explanatory introduction (“For look!”; Isa 26:21; 60:2; 65:17, 18: 66:15; Jer 1:15; 25:29; 30:10; 45:5; 46:27; 50:9; Ezek 30:9; 36:9; Zech 2:10; 3:8), or as an emphatic introduction (“Look!”; Jdgs 3:15; Isa 3:1; Jer 8:17; 30:3; 49:15; Hos 9:6; Joel 3:1 [HT 4:1]; Amos 4:2, 13; 6:11, 14; 9:9; Hab 1:6; Zech 2:9 [HT 2:13]; Zech 3:9; 11:16).
notes.13: (tn): Or “high places” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*יוצא ממקומו.* 
מכסא רחמים לכסא הדין: ודרך על:
rashi.eng: *comes forth from His place.* From the throne of mercy to the throne of justice.

rashi.heb:
*במותי ארץ.* 
על הרמים וגסי הרוח:
rashi.eng: *and tread upon the high places of the earth.* On the high and haughty hearted.

notes.14: (tn): Or “melt” (NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). This is a figurative description of earthquakes, landslides, and collapse of the mountains, rather than some sort of volcanic activity (note the remainder of the verse).
notes.15: (sn): The mountains will disintegrate…the valleys will be split in two. This imagery pictures an earthquake and accompanying landslide.
notes.16: (tn): The words “the mountains will melt” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The simile extends back to the first line of the verse.
notes.17: (tn): The words “the rocks will slide down” are supplied in the translation for clarification. This simile elaborates on the prior one and further develops the imagery of the verse’s first line.

rashi.heb:
*כדונג.* 
שעוה:
rashi.eng: *like wax.* Heb. כַּדּוֹנַג. In mishnaic Hebrew, this is שַּׁעֲוָה

rashi.heb:
*מוגרים במורד.* 
ת"י דאשידין במודרון מוגרים לשון זיבת מים וכן (איכה ג׳:מ״ט) עיני נגרה נגרות ביום אפו (איוב כ׳:כ״ח) פרץ נחל מעם גר (שם כח) ויגר מזה (תלי' עה):
rashi.eng: *as water poured down a steep place.* Heb. מֻגָּרִים. Jonathan renders: poured down a steep place. מְגֻרִים is an expression of the running of water. Cf. (Lam. 3:49) “My eye trickles down (נִגְרָה;” (Job 20:28) “Shall flow away (נִגָרוֹת) on the day of His wrath;” (ibid. 28:4) “He breaks open a water course from the place it flows (גָּר);” (Ps. 75:9) “And He pours out (וַיַגֵּר) of this.”

notes.18: (tn, Heb): “and because of.” This was simplified in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.20: (tn, Heb): “What is the rebellion of Jacob?”
notes.21: (tn, Heb): “Is it not Samaria?” The negated rhetorical question expects the answer, “It certainly is!” To make this clear the question has been translated as a strong affirmative statement.
notes.23: (tn, Heb): “Is it not Jerusalem?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “It certainly is!” In vv. 2-5 Micah narrows the scope of God’s judgment from the nations (vv. 2-4) to his covenant people (v. 5). Universal judgment is coming, but ironically Israel is the focal point of God’s anger. In v. 5c the prophet includes Judah within the scope of divine judgment, for it has followed in the pagan steps of the northern kingdom. He accomplishes this with rhetorical skill. In v. 5b he develops the first assertion of v. 5a (“All of this is because of Jacob’s rebellion”). One expects in v. 5c an elaboration of the second assertion in v. 5a (“and the sins of the nation of Israel”), which one assumes, in light of v. 5b, pertains to the northern kingdom. But the prophet specifies the “sins” as “high places” and makes it clear that “the nation of Israel” includes Judah. Verses 6-7 further develop v. 5b (judgment on the northern kingdom), while vv. 8-16 expand on v. 5c (judgment on Judah). For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.24: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.25: (tn, Heb): “into a planting place for vineyards.”
notes.26: (tn, Heb): “pour” (so NASB, NIV); KJV, NRSV “pour down”; NAB “throw down”; NLT “roll.”
notes.27: (tn, Heb): “her stones.” The term stones is a metonymy for the city walls whose foundations were constructed of stone masonry.
notes.28: (tn, Heb): “I will uncover her foundations.” The term “foundations” refers to the lower courses of the stones of the city’s outer fortification walls.

rashi.heb:
*לעי השדה.* 
ליגרי חקלן לשון גלים כמו יגר שהדותא:
rashi.eng: *into a heap in the field.* Heb. הַשָּׂדֶה לְעִי. Jonathan renders: לִדְגוֹרִין דְּחַקְלָא, an expression of heaps. Cf. (Gen. 31:47) “יְגַר שַׂהֲדוּתָא, the heap of the testimony.”

rashi.heb:
*והגרתי לגי אבניה.* 
והסחבתי כמו המוגרי' במורד:
rashi.eng: *and I will cast its stones down into the valley.* Heb. וְהִגַּרְתִּי, and I will drag, similar to (verse 4) “poured down (מֻגָּרִים) a steep place.”

notes.29: (tn, Heb): “and all her prostitute’s wages will be burned with fire.” The precious metal used by Samaria’s pagan worship centers to make idols are here compared to a prostitute’s wages because Samaria had been unfaithful to the Lord and prostituted herself to pagan gods, such as Baal.
notes.32: (tn): No object is specified in the Hebrew text; the words “the metal” are supplied from the context.
notes.33: (tn, Heb): “for from a prostitute’s wages she gathered, and to a prostitute’s wages they will return.” When the metal was first collected it was comparable to the coins a prostitute would receive for her services. The metal was then formed into idols, but now the Lord’s fiery judgment would reduce the metal images to their original condition.

rashi.heb:
*כי מאתנן זונה קבצה.* 
כל ההון הזה:
rashi.eng: *for from the hire of a harlot it gathered.* all these riches.

rashi.heb:
*ועד אתנן זונה ישובו.* 
ולטמיון כשאר אתנני זונה ישובו כל קבוציה ויונתן תרגם ולבית פלחי טעותא יתמסרון כל קבוציה:
rashi.eng: *and to the hire of a harlot shall they return.* And all its [Samaria’s] gatherings will be used up like other harlots’ hires. Jonathan renders: And to the house of the idol worshippers shall all its gatherings be delivered.

notes.34: (tn): The prophet is probably the speaker here.
notes.35: (tn): Or “stripped.” The precise meaning of this Hebrew word is unclear. It may refer to walking barefoot (see 2 Sam 15:30) or to partially stripping oneself (see Job 12:17-19).
notes.36: (tn, Heb): “naked.” This probably does not refer to complete nudity, but to stripping off one’s outer garments as an outward sign of the destitution felt by the mourner.
notes.40: (tn): Or perhaps “ostrich” (cf. ASV, NAB, NASB, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*שולל.* 
משתגע כשוטה בתמהון לב כמו (תהלים עו) אשתוללו אבירי לב (ישעיה נט) וסר מרע משתולל והתי"ו היא באה לשמש בתיבה בלשון מתפעל ונתפעל וכן הילוך תיבה שתחילת יסודה שי"ן או סמ"ך כשבאו עליו תי"ו בלשון מתפעל ונתפעל נכנסת תוך התיבה כמו משתולל אומר אני שהוא מלשון שוגג כמו (מלכים ב ד) לא תשלה אותי (שמואל ב י) על השל די יאמר שלו (דניאל ג):
rashi.eng: *I will go mad.* Heb. שׁוֹלָל, becoming mad like a mentally deranged person, with bewilderment. Cf. (Ps. 76:6) “The stout-hearted have become mad (אֱשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ);” (Isa. 59:15) “And he who turns away from evil is considered mad (מִשְׁתּוֹלֵל).” The ‘tav’ comes into the word to serve in the reflexive present and past. This is the normal pattern of a word whose first radical letter is ‘shin’ or ‘sammech’ when a ‘tav’ is added in the reflexive, either present or past, as in מִשְׁתּוֹלֵל. I say that it is an expression of error, as in (II Kings 4:28) “Do not mislead (תַשְׁלֶה) me;” (II Sam. 6:7) “For his error (הַשַּׁל);” (Dan. 3:29) “who speaks anything amiss (שָׁלוּ).”

notes.41: (tn, Heb): “her”; the referent (Samaria) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.42: (tc): The MT reads the plural “wounds”; the singular is read by the LXX, Syriac, and Vg. Or “wound.”
notes.45: (tn, Heb): “the gate.” Kings and civic leaders typically conducted important business at the city gate (see 1 Kgs 22:10 for an example), and the term is understood here to refer by metonymy to the leadership who would be present at the gate.
notes.46: (tn, Heb): “to Jerusalem.” The expression “it has contaminated” do not appear in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied to fill out the parallelism with the preceding line. For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*כי אנושה מכותיה.* 
כי חולה היא במכותיה כמו ויאנש (שמואל ב יב):
rashi.eng: *For she is mortally ill [from] her wounds.* Heb. אֱנוּשָׁה. For she is ill from her wounds. Cf. (II Sam. 12:15) “And it became mortally ill (וַיֵּאָנַשׁ.).”

notes.47: (tn, Heb): “Tell it not in Gath.” The Hebrew word for “tell” (נָגַד, nagad) sounds like the name of the city, Gath (גַּת, gat).
notes.48: (tn): The Hebrew infinitive absolute before the negated jussive emphasizes the prohibition.
notes.49: (tc, Heb): The translation assumes a masculine plural imperative. If one were to emend בְּבֵית (b�vet) to בֵית (vet), Beth Leaphrah would then be the addressee and the feminine singular imperative (see Qere) could be retained, “O Beth Leaphrah, sit in the dust.”�“roll about in mourning in the dust”; or “wallow about in mourning in the dust.” The verb פָּלַשׁ (palash, “roll about in mourning [in dust]”; HALOT 935 s.v. פלשׁ) is figurative (metonymy) for sitting as an outward sign of mourning. To sit in the dust was an outward sign of mourning. The name Beth Leaphrah means “house of dust.”

rashi.heb:
*בגת אל תגידו.* 
פן ישמחו לנו פלשתים:
rashi.eng: *Do not declare it in Gath.* lest the Philistines rejoice about us.

rashi.heb:
*בבית לעפרה.* 
עפרת אבי העזרי:
rashi.eng: *in the houses of Aphrah.* This is Ophrah of the Abiezrites (Jud. 6:11).

rashi.heb:
*עפר התפלשי.* 
ל' נופל על הלשון וכן יושבת שפיר עריה בשת וכן לא יצאה יושבת צאנן כולם לפי שם העיר לשון הקינה:
rashi.eng: *wallow in the dust.* Heb. הִתְפַּלָּשִׁי, a play on words with the name Philistia (פְּלֶשֶת). Similarly, (verse 11) “ You inhabitant of Shafir, with your private parts exposed.” Similarly, (verse 11) “The inhabitant of Zanaan has not gone forth.” In all of these, the language of the lamentation is according to the name of the city.

rashi.heb:
*התפלשי.* 
התגלגלי פתרונו לפי עניינו התעפרי:
rashi.eng: *wallow.* Heb. הִתְפַּלָּשִׁי, roll. According to the context, cover yourself with dust.

notes.50: (tn): The Hebrew participial form, which is feminine singular, is here used in a collective sense for the all the residents of the town. See GKC 394 �122.s.
notes.51: (sn): The place name Shaphir means “pleasant” in Hebrew.
notes.52: (tn): The imperatival form is used rhetorically, emphasizing that the inhabitants of Shaphir will pass by into exile.
notes.53: (tn, Heb): “have not come out”; NIV “will not come out”; NLT “dare not come outside.” The expression can’t leave their city alludes to a siege of the town. The place name Zaanan sounds like the verb “come out” (i.e., “can’t leave”) in Hebrew.
notes.54: (sn): The place name Beth Ezel means “house of nearness” or “house of proximity” in Hebrew.
notes.55: (tn, Heb): “the lamentation of Beth Ezel.” The following words could be the lamentation offered up by Beth Ezel (subjective genitive) or the mourning song sung over it (objective genitive).
notes.56: (tc): The form עֶמְדָּתוֹ (’emdato) should be emended to חֲמַדְּתוֹ (khamadto, “his (the conqueror’s) desire”). The precise meaning of the line is uncertain. The translation assumes: (a) the subject of the third masculine singular verb יִקַּח (yiqqakh, “he/it takes”) is the conqueror, (b) the second masculine plural suffix (“you”) on the preposition מִן (min, “from”) refers to the residents of Shaphir and Zaanan, (c) the final form עֶמְדָּתוֹ should be emended to חֲמַדְּתוֹ, “his (the conqueror’s) desire.”

rashi.heb:
*עברי לכם.* 
התחיל בלשון יחידות נקבה כמדבר אל כנסיה העיר כמו שנאמר יושבת שפיר כולם בשם כנסיה אחת ואמר לכם כמדבר אל הרבים שהרי לרבים הוא אומר:
rashi.eng: *Pass along your way.* Heb. עִבְרִי לָכֶם. He commences with an expression in the feminine singular, as used in addressing the people of the city, as it is said: “the inhabitant of Shafir” addressing them all in the name of one people. And then he says, “לָכֶם, along your way” as used in addressing many people, for he was speaking to the public.

rashi.heb:
*יושבת שפיר.* 
שם העיר:
rashi.eng: *the inhabitant of Shafir.* Shafir is the name of the city.

rashi.heb:
*עריה בשת.* 
גלויה בית הבשת כאשר נקראת שפיר שהוא שם נפל היוצא מרחמה של אשה:
rashi.eng: *with your private parts exposed.* Private parts would be exposed, appropriate to a city called “Shafir,” the name of the aborted fetus that comes out of the woman’s womb.

rashi.heb:
*לא יצאה יושבת צאנן.* 
לא יפקון משזבין יתבי צאנן:
rashi.eng: *the inhabitants of Zaanan did not go forth.* The fugitives of the inhabitants of Zaanan shall not go forth. - [from Jonathan]

rashi.heb:
*מספד בית האצל יקח מכם עמדתו.* 
המספד שגרמתם לנגזלים שאתם גוזלים נחלתו כדי להגיש בית בבית שדה בשדה זה אצל זה הוא יקח מכם עמדתו מעמד הבניינים שבנית' והעמדתם על נחלתם:
rashi.eng: *the lamentation caused by drawing the houses one to the other shall take its stand from you.* The lamentation you caused those who were robbed, whom you robbed of their inheritance in order to draw one house to the other, one field to the other, will take its stand from you - the stand of the houses that you built and erected on their inheritance.

rashi.heb:
*בית האצל.* 
איוטמנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *by drawing the houses from one the other.* ajoustement in Old French [which means, adding or joining].

notes.57: (sn): The place name Maroth sounds like the Hebrew word for “bitter.”
notes.58: (tc, Heb): The translation assumes an emendation of חָלָה (khalah; from חִיל, khil, “to writhe”) to יִחֲלָה (yikhalah; from יָחַל, yakhal, “to wait”). “[the residents of Maroth] writhe [= “anxiously long for”?] good.”
notes.59: (tn, Heb): “though disaster has come down from the Lord to the gate of Jerusalem.”

rashi.heb:
*כי חלה לטוב.* 
כי קיותה לטובה אותה היושבת בשלוותה וממרה ע"פ הנביאים:
rashi.eng: *For the one dwelling in disobedience hoped for good.* For the one dwelling in tranquility and disobeying the word of the prophets hoped for good.

rashi.heb:
*כי ירד רע.* 
הרי כי זה משמש בל' אלא היא חלה לטוב אבל מפני מרותה ירד לה רע:
rashi.eng: *but evil descended.* Heb. כִּי. This instance of כִּי serves as an expression of “but.” She hoped for good, but, because of her disobedience, evil descended to her.

notes.60: (sn): The place name Lachish sounds like the Hebrew word for “team [of horses].”
notes.61: (tn, Heb): “she”; this has been translated as second person (“you”) in keeping with the direct address to the residents of Lachish in the previous line.
notes.62: (sn): The epithet Daughter Zion pictures the city of Jerusalem as a young lady.
notes.63: (tn, Heb): “She was the beginning of sin for Daughter Zion.”
notes.64: (tn, Heb): “for in you was found the transgressions of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*רתום המרכבה לרכש.* 
אסרו המרכבה לרכש שהוא קל לרוץ ותברחו ואמר דונש שהוא ל' ערבי:
rashi.eng: *Hitch the chariot to the swift steeds.* Heb. רְתֹם הַמֶּרְכָּבָה לַרֶכֶשׁ. Hitch the chariot to the רֶכֶשׁ, which is swift to run, and you shall escape. The word רֶכֶשׁ is explained by Dunash (Teshuvoth Dunash p. 69) as an Arabic word.

notes.65: (tn): The subject of the feminine singular verb is probably Lachish.
notes.66: (tn, Heb): “you will give a dowry to”; NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “give parting gifts to.” Lachish is compared to a father who presents wedding gifts to his daughter as she leaves her father’s home to take up residence with her husband. In similar fashion Lachish will bid farewell to Moresheth Gath, for the latter will be taken by the invader.
notes.67: (tn, Heb): “houses.” By metonymy this refers to the people who live in them.
notes.68: (sn): The place name Achzib (אַכְזִיב, ’akhziv, “place on the dried up river”; see HALOT 45 s.v. אַכְזָב) creates a word play on the similar sounding term כָּזָב (kazav, “lie, deception”; HALOT 468 s.v. כָּזָב). Like the dried up river upon which its name was based, the city of Achzib would fail to help the kings of Israel in their time of need.
notes.69: (tn): Or “will be a deception.” The term אַכְזָב (’akhzav) is often translated “deception,” as derived from the verb I כָּזָב (“to deceive, lie”; HALOT 467-68 s.v. I כזב). However, it probably means “what is dried up,” since (1) the noun elsewhere refers to an empty well or dried river in summer (Jer 15:18; cf. Job 6:15-20) (HALOT 45 s.v. אַכְזָב); (2) the place-name “Achzib” (אַכְזִיב) literally means “place on the אַכְזָב [dried up river]” (HALOT 45 s.v. אַכְזָב); and (3) it is derived from the verb II כָּזָב (“to dry up [brook]”; Isa 58:11), which also appears in Mishnaic Hebrew and Arabic. The point of the metaphor is that Achzib will be as disappointing to the kings of Israel as a dried up spring in the summer is to a thirsty traveler in the Jordanian desert.
notes.70: (sn): Because of the enemy invasion, Achzib would not be able to deliver soldiers for the army and/or services normally rendered to the crown.

rashi.heb:
*לכן תתני שלוחים על מורשת גת.* 
על אשר תתני שלוחים על מלכות דוד אשר הוריש אתכם גת כענין שנאמר (ד"ה א יח) ויקח דוד את גת מיד פלשתים ואתם מואסים בו כמו שנאמר (ישעיה ח) יען אשר מאס העם הזה את מי השלוח וגומר לפיכך בתי אכזיב שהיתה מארץ יהודה ונמשכו אחר פקח בן רמליהו סופן להיות לאכזב למלכי ישראל שיהרג פקח בן רמליהו ויכזבו הנסמכים עליו ובימי אחז נתנבאת נבואה זו:
rashi.eng: *Since you give expulsions to the dynasty that gave you the possession of Gath.* Since you give expulsions to the kingdom of David, which gave you the possession of Gath, as the matter is stated (I Chron. 18:1): “And he took Gath and its cities out of the hands of the Philistines.” But you reject it, as it is stated (Isa. 8:6): “Since this people has rejected the waters of the Shiloah that flow gently, etc.” Therefore, “the houses of Achzib” which was of the land of Judah and was drawn after Pekah the son of Remaliah, shall ultimately be a “dried up spring” to the kings of Israel - for Pekah the son of Remaliah will be assassinated, and all those who relied on him will be disappointed. This prophecy was prophesied during Ahaz’s reign.

rashi.heb:
*לכן תתני שלוחים.* 
פי' לכן כמו על אשר כמו (שם יז) על כן תטעי נטעי נעמנים על אשר נטעתיך נטעי נעמנים ואת נהפכת לזמורות זר:
rashi.eng: *since you give expulsions.* Heb. לָכֵן. The definition of לָכֵן is עַל אֲשֶׁר, because of. Cf. (Isa. 17:10) “Because (עַל כֵּן) I planted you with pleasant saplings,” and you turned into a branch of a stranger.

rashi.heb:
*בתי אכזיב לאכזב.* 
ל' נופל על הלשון מאגדת חלק למדתי מדרש מקרא זה כך:
rashi.eng: *the houses of Achzib shall be a dried up spring.* Heb. לְאַכְזָב. This [too] is a play on words לְאַכְזָבת אַכְזִיב. I learned the midrash of this verse from the Aggadah of the chapter “Chelek.” [from Sanh. 102a]

notes.71: (sn): The place name Mareshah sounds like the Hebrew word for “conqueror.”
notes.72: (tn, Heb): “Again a conqueror I will bring to you, residents of Mareshah.” The first person verb is problematic, for the Lord would have to be the subject (cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). But the prophet appears to be delivering this lament and the Lord is referred to in the third person in v. 12. Consequently many emend the verb to a third person form (יָבוֹא, yavo’) and understand the “conqueror” as subject.
notes.73: (tn, Heb): “to Adullam the glory of Israel will go.” This probably means that the nation’s leadership will run for their lives and, like David of old, hide from their enemy in the caves of Adullam. Cf. NIV’s “He who is the glory of Israel will come to Adullam,” which sounds as if an individual is in view, and could be understood as a messianic reference.

rashi.heb:
*עוד היורש אביא לך.* 
אויבים שיורישו אותך את היושבת במרשה, יורש למרשה לשון נופל על הלשון:
rashi.eng: *I will yet bring the possessor to you.* The enemies, who will possess you, you who dwell in Mareshah. The possessor (הַיוֹרֵש) to Mareshah (מָרֵשָה) -another play on words.

rashi.heb:
*עד עדולם.* 
שהוא לפני' מן הגבול יסוג אחור ויבא כבוד ישראל שיכבשו העכו"ם מגבול' עד עדולם כן ת"י עד עדולם ייתון בתחום ארעא דישראל, ומדרש אגדה שמעתיו משמו של רבי מנחם:
rashi.eng: *up to Adullam.* (which is within the border) will the glory of Israel retreat and come, for the enemies shall conquer from their border up to Adullam. So did Jonathan render: Until Adullam shall they go up and enter the border of the land of Israel. And I heard a Midrash Aggadah in the name of Rabbi Menachem:

rashi.heb:
*עוד היורש אביא לך.* 
ראוים היו בני עילם לירש את ארץ ישראל שהוא היה בכור לבני שם ובשביל אהבת אבותיכ' הסיבותיה לבני ארפכשד עתה אביא את כשדים ואת בני עילם עליהם:
rashi.eng: *I will yet bring the heir.* The children of Elam were fit to inherit the land of Israel - for he [Elam] was the firstborn of the sons of Shem - but because of love for your forefathers I transferred it to the children of Arphachshad. Now I will bring the Chaldeans and the Elamites upon them.

notes.74: (tn, Heb): “over the sons of your delight.”
notes.76: (tn): Or “a vulture” (cf. NIV, TEV); CEV “a buzzard.” The Hebrew term נֶשֶׁר (nesher) refers to the griffon vulture or eagle.

rashi.heb:
*קרחי.* 
ראשך:
rashi.eng: *Make bald.* Make your head bald.

rashi.heb:
*וגוזי.* 
שערך כמו (איוב א) ויגז את ראשו לשון תלישת שער:
rashi.eng: *and crop.* your hair. Cf. (Job 1:20) “And he cropped (וָיָּגָז) his hair.” This is an expression of pulling out the hair.

rashi.heb:
*כנשר.* 
כתרגומו כנשרא דנתרו גדפוהי דרך הנשר למרט רוב כנפיו:
rashi.eng: *like an eagle.* As the Targum renders. Like an eagle, whose feathers have fallen out. It is customary for an eagle to lose most of its feathers.

notes.77: (tn, Heb): “Woe to those who plan sin.” The Hebrew term הוֹי (hoy, “woe”; “ah”) was a cry used in mourning the dead.
notes.78: (tn, Heb): “those who do evil upon their beds.”
notes.79: (tn, Heb): “at the light of morning they do it.”

rashi.heb:
*ופעולי רע על משכבותם.* 
כל הלילה גומרים בלבם איך יעשו הרעה לבקר:
rashi.eng: *and work evil on their bed.* All night they decide in their hearts how they will perform evil in the morning.

notes.80: (tn, Heb): “they desire fields and rob [them], and houses and take [them] away.”
notes.81: (tn, Heb): “and they oppress a man and his home.”
notes.82: (tn, Heb): “and a man and his inheritance.” The verb עָשַׁק (’ashaq, “to oppress”; “to wrong”) does double duty in the parallel structure and is understood by ellipsis in the second line.

rashi.heb:
*ובתים ונשאו.* 
מוסב על וחמדו חומדים בתים:
rashi.eng: *and houses, and they take.* This refers back to “and they covet.” They covet houses.

rashi.heb:
*ונשאו.* 
כמו ולקחו:
rashi.eng: *and they take.* Heb. וְנָשָׂאוּ, like וְלָקָחוּ, and they take.

notes.84: (tn, Heb): “from which you will not remove your neck.” The words “It will be like a yoke” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*ולא תלכו רומה.* 
ולא תהכון בקומה זקופה:
rashi.eng: *and you shall not walk erect.* You shall not walk with an upright stature.

notes.86: (tc, Heb): The form נִהְיָה (nihyah) should be omitted as dittographic (note the preceding וְנָהָה נְהִי v�nahah n�hiy). “one will lament [with] a lamentation [and] say.”
notes.87: (tn): Or “exchange.” The LXX suggests a reading יִמַּד (yimmad) from מָדַד (madad, “to measure”). In this case one could translate, “the property of my people is measured out [i.e., for resale].”
notes.88: (tn, Heb): “how one removes for me.” Apparently the preposition has the nuance “from” here (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
notes.89: (tc, Heb): The Hebrew term שׁוֹבֵב (shovev, “the one turning back”) elsewhere has the nuance “apostate” (cf. NASB) or “traitor” (cf. NIV). The translation assumes an emendation to שָׁבָה (shavah, “captor”). “to the one turning back he assigns our fields.”

rashi.heb:
*ונהה נהי נהיה.* 
ונהה ל' עתיד כמו ועשה ופנה ונהה המקונן ואמר נהי נהיה בעולם ומהו הנהי אשר נהיה אמר:
rashi.eng: *and he shall lament, “A lamentation has come about…”.* Heb. נְהִי נִהְיָה וְנָהָה. וְנָהָה is a future tense, like וְעָשָה, and he shall make, and וּפָנָה, and he shall turn. The lamenting one shall lament and say, “A lamentation has come about in the world. Now what is the lamentation that has come about?…”

rashi.heb:
*שדוד נשדונו.* 
אויבינו שדדונו. ולשון נשדנו שכתב בו נו"ן בתחילה ולא כתב שדונו מפני שבא לשמש שני לשונות ל' נפעלנו ולשון פעלנו אילו כתב נשדנו היה הל' מוסב על הנשדדים ולא אל השודדים ואם כתב שדונו היה מוסב אל השודדים ולא לנשדדים עכשיו מוסב לשניהם נתננו ביד אשר שדונו ובלע"ז שומי"ר דימשטיור"א נשו"ט, ד"א נשדונו אנחנו גרמנו לעצמינו ששדדונו:
rashi.eng: *They have robbed us!.* Heb. שָׁדוֹד נְשַׁדֻּנוּ. Our enemies have robbed us, The prophet uses the expression נְשַׁדֻּנוּ, in which there is a “nun” in the beginning, and does not use שַׁדוּנוּ, because נְשַׁדֻּנוּ serves in two voices, the passive voice and the active voice. Had the prophet written נְשַדֹנוּ, in the passive voice, the expression would refer to the robbed and not to the robbers. Had he written שַדוּנוּ, in the active voice, the expression would refer to the robbers and not to the robbed. This way, it refers to both: we were given into the hand of those who robbed us. In Old French, there is the expression somes degatert nous, we were ravaged. Another explanation: נְשַׁדֻּנוּ means we brought upon ourselves that they robbed us.

rashi.heb:
*חלק עמי ימיר.* 
נחלת חלק עמי נחלף לעכו"ם:
rashi.eng: *He changes the portion of my people.* The inheritance of the portion of my people has been exchanged to the enemy.

rashi.heb:
*איך ימיש לי לשובב שדינו יחלק.* 
איך יסור אלי עוד להשיב לנו שדותינו אשר יחלק אותם העכו"ם הזה לו איך אפשר לשובב' עוד לי כל אלה דברי המקונן ונושא המשל:
rashi.eng: *How will He turn to me to return our fields, which he divides.* How will He turn again to me, to return our fields to us, which this enemy divides for himself? How is it possible to return them to me anymore? All these are the words of the lamenting one who takes up the parable.

rashi.heb:
*איך ימיש לי .* 
קומ"א שדיטורנר"א אמו"י כמו סורה אלי ויסור אליו:
rashi.eng: *How will He turn to me.* Kome se destornera amois? As in (Jud. 4:18) “Turn to me…. And he turned to her.”

notes.90: (tn, Heb): “therefore you will not have one who strings out a measuring line by lot in the assembly of the Lord.” No one will assign you land in the Lord’s community. When judgment passes and the people are restored to the land, those greedy ones who disregarded the ancient land allotments will not be allowed to participate in the future redistribution of the land.

rashi.heb:
*משליך חבל.* 
חולק נחלה שכן דרך לחלק נחלה בחבל המדה:
rashi.eng: *who casts a line.* Divides a heritage. It is customary to divide a heritage with a measuring line.

notes.91: (tn, Heb): “‘Do not foam at the mouth,’ they foam at the mouth.” The verb נָטַף (nataf) means “to drip.” When used of speech it probably has the nuance “to drivel, to foam at the mouth” (HALOT 694 s.v. נטף). The sinful people tell the Lord’s prophets not to “foam at the mouth,” which probably refers in a derogatory way to their impassioned style of delivery. But the Lord (who is probably still speaking here, see v. 3) sarcastically refers to their impassioned exhortation as “foaming at the mouth.”
notes.92: (tc, Heb): If one follows the MT as it stands, it would appear that the Lord here condemns the people for their “foaming at the mouth” and then announces that judgment is inevitable. The present translation assumes that this is a continuation of the quotation of what the people say. In this case the subject of “foam at the mouth” is the Lord’s prophets. In the second line יִסַּג (yissag, a Niphal imperfect from סוּג, sug, “to remove”) is emended to יַסִּגֵנוּ (yassigenu; a Hiphil imperfect from נָסַג/נָשַׂג, nasag/nasag, “to reach; to overtake”). “they should not foam at the mouth concerning these things, humiliation will not be removed.”

rashi.heb:
*אל תטיפו יטיפון.* 
אל תנבאו להוכיחם לכם הנביאים אני אומר אשר תטיפו תמיד:
rashi.eng: *“Preach not, those who preach”.* Do not prophesy to reprove them. To you, the prophets who constantly preach, I say this.

rashi.heb:
*לא יסג כלמות.* 
פן ישיגון אתכם כלימות מאתם כענין שנאמר (משלי ט׳:ח׳) אל תוכח לץ, כל טיף לשון נבואה כמו (עמוס ז׳:ט״ז) ולא תטיף על בית ישחק, (יחזקאל כ״א:ב׳) והטף אל דרום:
rashi.eng: *they shall not take shame.* Lest disgraces from them overtake them, as the matter is stated (Prov. 9:8): “Reprove not a scorner.” Every instance of טִיף is an expression of prophecy, as in (Amos 7:16) “And do not prophesy (תַטִיף) concerning the house of Isaac” and (Ezek. 21:2) “And prophesy (וְהַטֵף) to the south.”

notes.94: (tc): The MT has אָמוּר (’amur), an otherwise unattested passive participle, which is better emended to אָמוֹר (’amor), an infinitive absolute functioning as a finite verb (see BDB 55 s.v. אָמַר).
notes.95: (tn): The Hebrew word רוּחַ (ruach) often means “Spirit” when used of the Lord, but here it seems to have an abstract sense, “patience.” See BDB 925 s.v. 3.d.
notes.96: (tn, Heb): “Has the patience of the Lord run short? Or are these his deeds?” The rhetorical questions expect the answer, “No, of course not.” The people contest the prophet’s claims that the Lord’s judgment is falling on the nation.
notes.97: (tn, Heb): “Do not my words accomplish good for the one who walks uprightly?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course they do!” The Lord begins his response to the claim of the house of Jacob that they are immune to judgment (see v. 7a). He points out that the godly are indeed rewarded, but then he goes on to show that those in the house of Jacob are not godly and can expect divine judgment, not blessing (vv. 8-11). Some emend “my words” to “his words.” In this case, v. 7b is a continuation of the immediately preceding quotation. The people, thinking they are godly, confidently ask, “Do not his [God’s] words accomplish good for the one who walks uprightly?”

rashi.heb:
*האמור בית יעקב.* 
הזאת יאמרו בית יעקב כששומעים את הרעה אשר נביאי מתנבאים להם:
rashi.eng: *Is that what is said by the house of Jacob?.* Do (the people of) the house of Jacob say this when they hear the evil that my prophets prophesy for them?

rashi.heb:
*הקצר רוח ה'.* 
שמא אין יכולת עתה לפניו להטיב ואין רוחו רחבה עליו לטוב כאשר היתה בימים הראשונים:
rashi.eng: *Has the Lord’s patience grown short?.* Is He now unable to do good, or does He not (now) have the patience that He had in the early days to do good?

rashi.heb:
*אם אלה מעלליו.* 
כלו' להרע:
rashi.eng: *Are these His deeds?.* I.e., to do evil?

rashi.heb:
*הלא דברי ייטיבו עם הישר הולך.* 
אני לא קצרה רוחי ולא אלה מעללי זולתי לרשעים אך את הישר הולך היטב אטיב לו:
rashi.eng: *Do not My words benefit the one who goes straight?.* I am not impatient, neither are these My deeds, except to the wicked; but with the one who goes straight, I do good.

notes.98: (tc, Heb): “Recently my people rise up as an enemy.” The MT is problematic in light of v. 9, where “my people” are the object of oppression, not the perpetrators of it. The form וְאֶתְמוּל (v�’etmul, “and recently”) is probably the product of fusion and subsequent suppression of an (ע) ayin. The translation assumes an emendation to וְאַתֶּם עַל (v�’attem ’al, “and you against [my people]”). The second person plural pronoun fits well with the second plural verb forms of vv. 8b-10. If this emendation is accepted, then יְקוֹמֵם (y�qomem, the imperfect of קוּם [qum]) should be emended to קָמִים (qamim; a participle from the same root).
notes.99: (tc, Heb): “From the front of a garment glory [or perhaps, “a robe”] you strip off,” but this makes little if any sense. The term מִמּוּל (mimmul, “from the front of”) is probably the product of dittography (note the preceding word, which ends in [ם] mem) and subsequent suppression of ע (ayin). The translation assumes an emendation to מֵעַל (me’al, “from upon”). The translation also assumes an emendation of שַׂלְמָה אֶדֶר (salmah ’eder, “a garment, glory [or robe]”) to שֹׁלְמִים אֲדֶרֶת (shol�mim ’aderet, “[from] a friend the robe [you strip off]”). The MT’s אֶדֶר (’eder) is the result of misdivision (the article has erroneously been attached to the preceding word) and haplography (of the final tav, which also begins the following word).
notes.100: (tc, Heb): The passive participle שׁוּבֵי (shuvey) is unattested elsewhere and should be emended to a participle שָׁבִים (shavim). “from those passing by peacefully, returnees from war.” Actual refugees, however, are probably not in view. The second line compares those who pass by peacefully with individuals returning from war. The battle is over and they do not expect their own countrymen to attack them.

rashi.heb:
*ואתמול עמי לאויב יקומם.* 
המקרא מחובר לשל מעלה הימנו אני טוב ומטיב אני ואת הדבר אשר למולו ובעבורו עמי אותו יקומם לאויב לו:
rashi.eng: *And the matter for which My people causes [Me] to rise as an enemy.* Heb. וְאֶתְמוּל. The verse is connected to the one preceding it. I am good and do good, but the matter for which and because of which My people make me rise as an enemy to them…

rashi.heb:
*ממול שלמה אדר תפשיטון.* 
כנגד אשר אתם גוזלים השלמה ולבוש תפארת ומפשיטים מעל כל העוברים עליכם בדרך:
rashi.eng: *because of the garment, and the mantle that you strip.* Because you rob the garment, and you strip the glorious raiment from all those who pass you by on the road.

rashi.heb:
*מעוברים בטח שובי מלחמה.* 
ממה שהיו סבורין להיות עוברין בטח הם נהפכו להיות שובי מלחמה כבני אדם השבים מן המלחמה חסירי מבגדים ומזון שלקחו אויביהם מה שעליהם:
rashi.eng: *from those who pass by confidently, who return from war.* Instead of passing by confidently, as they expected to, they became like men returning from war without clothing or food, for their enemies took everything they had.

rashi.heb: *שובי.*  כמו (ירמיהו ב׳:כ״א) סורי הגפן נכריה (צפניה ג) נוגי ממועד:
rashi.eng: *who return.* Heb. שׁוּבִי, as in (Jer. 2:21) “A degenerate (סוּרֵי) wild vine” and (Zeph. 3:18) “Those taken away (נוּגֵי) from the appointed season.”

notes.101: (tn, Heb): “women.” This may be a synecdoche of the whole (women) for the part (widows).
notes.102: (tn, Heb): “her little children” or “her infants”; ASV, NRSV “young children.”
notes.103: (tn, Heb): “from their children you take my glory forever.” The yod (י) ending on הֲדָרִי (hadariy) is usually taken as a first person common singular suffix (“my glory”). But it may be the archaic genitive ending (“glory of”) in the construct expression “glory of perpetuity,” that is, “perpetual glory.” In either case, this probably refers to the dignity or honor the Lord bestowed on each Israelite family by giving them a share of his land to be inherited perpetually from one generation to another within each family. The term הָדָר (hadar) may refer to possessions that a person prizes (Lam 1:6).

rashi.heb:
*נשי עמי תגרשון מבית תענוגיה.* 
שאתם הורגים את בעליהן והן יושבות אלמנו' או לפי שאתם נוטלין את ממון בעליהם והם יושבים ומצירים ואין משמחין את נשותיהן:
rashi.eng: *The wives of My people you drive away from the house of her delights.* For you slay their husbands, and they sit as widows. Alternatively: since you take their husband’s money, and they (the husbands) sit and grieve and do not bring joy to their wives.

rashi.heb:
*תקחו הדרי.* 
הדר הוד ועושר שנתתי להם:

notes.104: (tn, Heb): “Arise and go!” These imperatives are rhetorical. Those who wrongly drove widows and orphans from their homes and land inheritances will themselves be driven out of the land (cf. Isa 5:8-17). This is an example of poetic justice.
notes.105: (tn, Heb): “for this is no resting place.” The Lord speaks to the oppressors.
notes.106: (tn, Heb): “uncleanness will destroy, and destruction will be severe.”

rashi.heb:
*קומו ולכו כי לא זאת המנוחה.* 
קומו וגלו מן הארץ כי לא כדרך זו נתתיה לכם למנוחה:
rashi.eng: *Arise and go, for this is not the tranquility.* Arise and go into exile from the land, for it was not in this manner that I gave it to you for tranquility.

rashi.heb:
*בעבור טמאה תחבל וחבל נמרץ.* 
כי למען טמא אותה היא עוש' חבורת חבלי רשעים:
rashi.eng: *in order to contaminate it, it forms bands, and the band is clarified.* In order to contaminate it [the land], it [the people] forms a band of groups of wicked men.

rashi.heb:
*תחבל.* 
לשון אגודות כמו (שמואל א י׳:ה׳) חבל נביאים (תהילים קי״ט:ס״א) חבלי רשעים וכן ת"י מסתיעין עלה לשון סיעה:
rashi.eng: *it forms bands.* Heb. תְּחַבֵּל. This is an expression of companies, as in (I Sam. 10:5) “a band (חֶבֶל) of prophets”; (Ps. 119:61) “Bands of (חֶבְלֵי) wicked men.” And so did Jonathan render: And they band together upon it, an expression of a band.

rashi.heb:
*וחבל נמרץ.* 
ובעת אגודתם כבר נועצו ביניהם ופירשו למה הם מתחברים:
rashi.eng: *and the band is clarified.* Heb. וְחֶבֶל נִמְרָץ. And at the time of their banding together, they already took counsel among themselves and explained for what purpose they were banding together.

rashi.heb:
*נמרץ.* 
דבר מפורש באר היטב כמו (איוב ו׳:כ״ה) מה נמרצו אמרי מה ימריצך (שם טז) קללה נמרצת (מלכים א ב):
rashi.eng: *clarified.* Heb. נִמְרָץ. A thing explained clearly, as in (Job 6:25) “How clear (נִמְרְצוּ) are right words;” (ibid. 16:3) “What clarifies (יַמְרִיצְךָ) to you;” (I Kings 2:8) “A clear (נִמְרֶצֶת) curse.”

notes.107: (tn, Heb): “if a man, coming [as] wind and falsehood, should lie”; NASB “walking after wind and falsehood”; NIV “a liar and a deceiver.”
notes.108: (tn, Heb): “I will foam at the mouth concerning wine and beer.”
notes.109: (tn, Heb): “he would be the foamer at the mouth for this people.”

rashi.heb:
*לו איש הולך רוח.* 
לו מוצאים איש הולך רוח איש שקר מתנבא להם שישתכרו ביין ובשכר הוא יהיה נביא מקובל לעם הזה:
rashi.eng: *If a man walking in wind.* If they (the people) would find a man walking in wind, a false man prophesying to them that they become drunk with wine and strong drink, he would be an acceptable prophet to this people.

notes.111: (tc): The MT reads בָּצְרָה (batsrah, “Bozrah”) but the form should be emended to בַּצִּרָה (batsirah, “into the fold”). See D. R. Hillers, Micah (Hermeneia), 38.
notes.112: (tc): The MT reads “its pasture,” but the final vav (ו) belongs with the following verb. See GKC 413 �127.i.
notes.113: (tn, Heb): “and they will be noisy [or perhaps, “excited”] from men.” The subject of the third feminine plural verb תְּהִימֶנָה (t�himenah, “they will be noisy”) is probably the feminine singular צֹאן (tso’n, “flock”). (For another example of this collective singular noun with a feminine plural verb, see Gen 30:38.) In the construction מֵאָדָם (me’adam, “from men”) the preposition is probably causal. L. C. Allen translates “bleating in fear of men” (Joel, Obadiah, Jonah, and Micah [NICOT], 300), but it is possible to take the causal sense as “because of the large quantity of men.” In this case the sheep metaphor and the underlying reality are mixed.

rashi.heb:
*אסוף אאסוף.* 
עוד ימים באים ואקבץ אתכם:
rashi.eng: *I will surely assemble.* Days will yet come when I will assemble you.

rashi.heb:
*כצאן בצרה.* 
כצאן רבה הנתונה במבצרי גדרות צאן:
rashi.eng: *as sheep in a fold.* Like many sheep placed in the fortresses of the sheep folds.

rashi.heb:
*בתוך הדברו.* 
ת"י כעדרא בגו דירא מקום שהוא מתנהג שם וכן (ישעיה ה) ורעו כבשים כדברם:
rashi.eng: *within its stall.* Heb. הַדָּבְרוֹ. Jonathan renders: And as a flock within a stall, the place where they are led; and likewise (Isa. 5:17): “And lambs shall graze as their wont (כְּדָבְרָם).”

rashi.heb:
*תהימנה מאדם.* 
תהיינה הערים הומיות מרוב אדם אשר בקרבה:
rashi.eng: *shall stir with people.* The cities shall be noisy because of the large number of people in their midst.

notes.114: (tn, Heb): “the one who breaks through goes up before them.” The verb form is understood as a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of this coming event.
notes.115: (tn): The three verb forms (a perfect and two preterites with vav [ו] consecutive) indicate certitude. The “fold” from which the sheep/people break out is probably a reference to their place of exile.
notes.116: (tn): The verb form (a preterite with vav [ו] consecutive) indicates certitude.
notes.117: (tn, Heb): “the Lord [will be] at their head.”

rashi.heb:
*עלה הפורץ.* 
מושיעם הפורץ גדרת סירים ומסוכות חדקים ליישר לפניהם הדרך:
rashi.eng: *The breaker has gone up.* Their savior, who breaks the fences of thorns and the hedges of briers, to straighten the road before them.

notes.120: (tn, Heb): “Should you not know justice?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course you should!”

notes.124: (tn, Heb): “their skin from upon them.” The referent of the pronoun (“my people,” referring to Jacob and/or the house of Israel, with the Lord as the speaker) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.125: (tn, Heb): “and their flesh from their bones.” Micah compares the social injustice perpetrated by the house of Jacob/Israel to cannibalism, because it threatens the very lives of the oppressed.

rashi.heb:
*גוזלי עורם.* 
של בית ישראל שהם ראשים וקצינים עליהם כמו שאמר ראשי בית יעקב וקציני בית ישראל:
rashi.eng: *who rob their skin.* [I.e., the skin] of the house of Israel, over whom they are heads and officers, as the prophet says: The heads of the house of Jacob and the officers of the house of Israel.

notes.127: (tc): The MT reads “and they chop up as in a pot.” The translation assumes an emendation of כַּאֲשֶׁר (ka’asher, “as”) to כִּשְׁאֵר (kish’er, “like flesh”).

rashi.heb:
*שאר עמי.* 
בשר עמי:
rashi.eng: *the flesh of My people.* Heb. שְׁאֵר עַמִּי.

rashi.heb:
*ואת עצמותיהם פצחו.* 
פתחו להוציא המוח כמו (שם יד) פצחו רנה פתחו פה ברנה:
rashi.eng: *and opened their bones.* Heb. פִצֵּחוּ. They opened [them] to take out the marrow. Cf. (Isa. 14:7) “They opened (פָצְחוּ) in song” -they opened their mouth in song.

rashi.heb:
*ופרשו כאשר בסיר.* 
ומשברים האברים כאשר ישברו הנתחים הניתנים בסיר לבשל:
rashi.eng: *and broke [them] as in a pot.* Heb. וּפָרְשׁוּ. They break the limbs as they break the cuts [of meat] in a pot to cook [them].

rashi.heb:
*ופרשו.* 
לשון שבר כמו פרוש לרעב (שם נח) ולא יפרשו להם (ירמיה טז) פרשיה ציון (איכה א):
rashi.eng: *and broke.* Heb. וּפָרְשׁוּ, an expression of breaking. Cf. (Isa. 58:7) “To share (פָרֹס) with the hungry;” (Jer. 16:7) “And they shall not break [bread] (יִפְרְסוּ) for them;” (Lam. 1:17) “Zion broke (פֵּרְשָה).”

rashi.heb:
*קלחת.* 
קלדיי"רא בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *a cauldron.* Heb. קַלַחַת, kaldere in O.F.

notes.128: (tn, Heb): “then they will cry out to the Lord.” The words “Someday these sinners” have been supplied in the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*אז יזעקו אל ה'.* 
אז בבא אותו העת האמור למעלה אסף אאסף יעקב יזעקו אל ה' להטיב להם ברצון עמו ושמחת גויו ולא יענה אותם:
rashi.eng: *Then they shall cry out to the Lord.* Then, when that time mentioned above, [that] “I will surely assemble Jacob,” comes, they shall cry out to the Lord to do good for them with the will of His people and with the joy of His nation, but He shall not respond to them.

notes.129: (tn, Heb): “concerning the prophets, those who mislead my people.” The first person pronominal suffix is awkward in a quotation formula that introduces the words of the Lord. For this reason some prefer to begin the quotation after “the Lord says” (cf. NIV), but this leaves “concerning the prophets” hanging very awkwardly at the beginning of the quotation. It is preferable to add הוֹי (hoy, “woe, ah”) at the beginning of the quotation, right after the graphically similar יְהוָה (y�hvah; see D. R. Hillers, Micah [Hermeneia], 44). The phrase הוֹי עַל (hoy ’al, “woe upon”) occurs in Jer 50:27 and Ezek 13:3 (with “the prophets” following the preposition in the latter instance).
notes.130: (tn, Heb): “those who bite with their teeth and cry out, ‘peace.’” The phrase “bite with the teeth” is taken here as idiomatic for eating. Apparently these prophets were driven by mercenary motives. If they were paid well, they gave positive oracles to their clients, but if someone could not afford to pay them, they were hostile and delivered oracles of doom.
notes.131: (tn, Heb): “but [as for the one] who does not place [food] in their mouths, they prepare for war against him.”

rashi.heb:
*הנושכים בשיניהם.* 
ואוכלים בשר בהמו' פטומות המאכילים אותם עמי הטועים אחריהם:
rashi.eng: *who bite with their teeth.* and eat the flesh of fattened animals, which my people who stray after them feed them.

rashi.heb:
*וקראו שלום.* 
וכאשר יאכילו יקראו ויתנבאו להם שלום:
rashi.eng: *and herald peace.* And, when they feed them, they herald and prophesy peace for them.

rashi.heb:
*וקדשו עליו מלחמה.* 
והזמינו עליו למלחמה:
rashi.eng: *they prepare war.* Heb. וְקִדְּשׁוּ.

notes.132: (tn, Heb): “it will be night for you without a vision.” The coming of night (and darkness in the following line) symbolizes the cessation of revelation.
notes.133: (tn, Heb): “it will be dark for you without divination.” The reading of omens ( “divination”) was forbidden in the law (Deut 18:10), so this probably reflects the prophets’ view of how they received divine revelation.
notes.134: (tn, Heb): “and the day will be dark over them.”

notes.136: (tn): Or “the mustache,” or perhaps “the beard.” Cf. KJV, NAB, NRSV “cover their lips.”
notes.137: (tn, Heb): “for there will be no answer from God.”

rashi.heb:
*מענה אלהים.* 
מענה נקוד קמץ (ר"ל ציר"י) לפי שהוא דבוק אל השם:
rashi.eng: *statement of God.* Heb. מַעֲנֵה is vowelized with a kamatz [meaning a zeirah] since it is attached to God’s Name.

notes.138: (sn): The prophet Micah speaks here and contrasts himself with the mercenaries just denounced by the Lord in the preceding verses.
notes.139: (tn, Heb): “am full of power, the Spirit of the Lord, and justice and strength.” The appositional phrase “the Spirit of the Lord” explains the source of the prophet’s power. The phrase “justice and strength” is understood here as a hendiadys, referring to the prophet’s strong sense of justice.
notes.140: (tn, Heb): “to declare to Jacob his rebellion and to Israel his sin.” The words “this enables me” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

notes.143: (tn, Heb): “who.” A new sentence was begun here in the translation for stylistic reasons (also at the beginning of v. 10).

notes.146: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.147: (sn): The pronoun Her refers to Jerusalem (note the previous line).
notes.149: (tn, Heb): “they lean upon” (so KJV, NIV, NRSV); NAB “rely on.”
notes.150: (tn, Heb): “Is not the Lord in our midst?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course he is!”
notes.151: (tn): Or “come upon” (so many English versions); NCV “happen to us”; CEV “come to us.”

notes.152: (tn): The plural pronoun refers to the leaders, priests, and prophets mentioned in the preceding verse.
notes.154: (tn, Heb): “the mountain of the house” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*עיין.* 
דגורין:
rashi.eng: *Jerusalem shall become heaps.* Heb. עִיּין.

notes.157: (tn, Heb): “will be established as the head of the mountains.”
notes.158: (tn, Heb): “it will be lifted up above the hills.”

rashi.heb:
*ונהרו.* 
ונקבצו שם יחד כנהרו' ההולכי' אל הים:
rashi.eng: *shall stream.* Heb. וְנָהֲרוּ. And they shall gather there together like rivers flowing into the sea.

notes.161: (tn, Heb): “and we can walk in his paths.”
notes.162: (tn, Heb): “instruction [or, “law”] will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.” For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.164: (tn): Or “mighty” (NASB); KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV “strong”; TEV “among the great powers.”
notes.165: (tn, Heb): “[for many nations] to a distance.”
notes.166: (sn): Instead of referring to the large plow as a whole, the plowshare is simply the metal tip which actually breaks the earth and cuts the furrow.
notes.167: (sn): This implement was used to prune the vines, i.e., to cut off extra leaves and young shoots (M. Klingbeil, NIDOTTE 1:1117-18). It was a short knife with a curved hook at the end sharpened on the inside like a sickle.

rashi.heb:
*ושפט.* 
משפט זה לשון תוכחה הוא דשרימנ"ט בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *And he shall judge.* This judgment is an expression of reproof, derajjnement in O.F. [Isa 2:4]

notes.169: (tn, Heb): “and there will be no one making [him] afraid.”
notes.170: (tn, Heb): “for the mouth of the Lord of Hosts has spoken.”

rashi.heb:
*כי פי ה' צבאות דבר.* 
והיכן דבר ונתתי שלום בארץ (ויקרא כ״ו:ו׳):
rashi.eng: *for the mouth of the Lord of Hosts has spoken.* Now where has He spoken? (Lev. 26:6) “And I will place peace in the land, etc.” [from Mechilta to Exodus 12:25]

notes.171: (tn, Heb): “walk each in the name of his god.” The term “name” here has the idea of “authority.” To “walk in the name” of a god is to recognize the god’s authority as binding over one’s life.

rashi.heb:
*ילכו איש בשם אלהיו.* 
ילכו לאבדון על שעבדו עכו"ם כן תירגם יונתן:
rashi.eng: *For all peoples shall go, each one in the name of his god.* Shall go to destruction because they worshipped idols. So did Jonathan render it.

notes.173: (sn): The exiles of the nation are compared to lame and injured sheep.

rashi.heb:
*אוספה הצולעה.* 
אכניש מטלטליא וכן ת"י, ולי נראה לשון מרפא כמו ואספתי מצרעתו (מלכים ה):
rashi.eng: *I will heal the limping one.* Heb. אֹסְפָה. I will gather in the exiles. So did Jonathan render. To me, however, it appears as an expression of healing, as in (II Kings 5:6) “And you shall cure him (וְאֲסַפְתּוֹ) of his zaraath.”

rashi.heb:
*ואשר הריעותי.* 
ואותם שהריעותי להם בעוונם:
rashi.eng: *and those whom I harmed.* And those whom I harmed because of their iniquity.

notes.174: (tn, Heb): “make the lame into a remnant.”
notes.175: (tn): The precise meaning of this difficult form is uncertain. The present translation assumes the form is a Niphal participle of an otherwise unattested denominative verb הָלָא (hala’, “to be far off”; see BDB 229 s.v.), but attractive emendations include הַנַּחֲלָה (hannakhalah, “the sick one[s]”) from חָלָה (khalah) and הַנִּלְאָה (hannil’ah, “the weary one[s]”) from לָאָה (la’ah).

notes.177: (tn, Heb): “Migdal-eder.” Some English versions transliterate this phrase, apparently because they view it as a place name (cf. NAB).
notes.178: (sn): The city of David, located within Jerusalem, is addressed as Daughter Zion. As the home of the Davidic king, who was Israel’s shepherd (Ps 78:70-72), the royal citadel could be viewed metaphorically as the watchtower of the flock.
notes.179: (tn, Heb): “to you it will come, the former dominion will arrive.”

rashi.heb:
*ואתה מגדל עדר.* 
ת"י ואת משיחא דישראל דטמיר מן קדם חובי כנישתא דציון פי' מגדל ל' מעוז ותרגום עדר כנסת ישראל ותירגם עופל ל' אופל ויש לפרש מגדל עדר בית המקדש ועופל לשון מגדל עוז וכן עופל ובחן (ישעיה לב):
rashi.eng: *And you, tower of the flock.* Heb. מִגְדַּל עֵדֶר. Jonathan renders: And you, anointed one of Israel, who is hidden because of the sins of the people of Zion. His explanation is: מִגְדַּל is an expression of a stronghold, and he renders עֵדֶר as the people of Israel. He renders עֹפֶל as an expression of אֹפֶל, darkness. [I.e., מִגְדַּל עֵדֶר is the stronghold of Israel, identified as the Messiah. He is hidden because of the sins of the people of Zion. The word “hidden” is derived from אֹפֶל, darkness.] But it is possible to interpret מִגְדַּל עֵדֶר as the Temple, and עֹפֶל as an expression of a mighty tower. Likewise there is (Isa. 32:14) “Rampart (עֹפֶל) and tower.”

rashi.heb:
*עדיך תאתה.* 
שארית הצולעה והנהלאה כולם יקבצו אליך:
rashi.eng: *to you it shall come.* The remnant of the limping ones and the scattered ones shall gather to you.

rashi.heb:
*ובאה הממשלה הראשונה.* 
תבא הממשלה שלימה כולה אל בית דוד בירושלים כאשר היתה בתחילה עד שלא נחלקה ומה היא הממשלה הראשונ' הממלכ' לבת ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *and the former kingdom shall come.* The complete kingdom, in its entirety, shall come to the house of David in Jerusalem as it was originally, before it was divided. Now what was the former kingdom? The kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

notes.180: (tn): The Hebrew form is feminine singular, indicating that Jerusalem, personified as a young woman, is now addressed (see v. 10). In v. 8 the tower/fortress was addressed with masculine forms, so there is clearly a shift in addressee here. “Jerusalem” has been supplied in the translation at the beginning of v. 9 to make this shift apparent.
notes.181: (tn, Heb): “Now why are you shouting [with] a shout.”
notes.182: (tn, Heb): “Is there no king over you?”
notes.183: (tn): Traditionally, “counselor” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV). This refers to the king mentioned in the previous line; the title points to the king’s roles as chief strategist and policy maker, both of which required extraordinary wisdom.
notes.184: (tn, Heb): “that.” The Hebrew particle כִּי (ki) is used here in a resultative sense; for this use see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 73, �450.

rashi.heb:
*עתה.* 
שאת מורדת בי:
rashi.eng: *Now.* that you rebel against Me.

rashi.heb:
*למה תריעי רע.* 
שיתי לבך למה את צריכה לבקש רעים ואהובים מלכי מצרים ומלכי אשור לעזור:
rashi.eng: *why do you seek friends?.* Heb. תָרִיעִי רֵעַ, lit. befriend a friend. Put to your heart: why do you need to seek friends and beloved ones, the kings of Egypt and the kings of Assyria, for aid?

notes.188: (tn, Heb): “hand.” The Hebrew idiom is a metonymy for power or control.

rashi.heb:
*חולי.* 
ל' חלחלה כמו (כאן) כי החזיקך חיל והלשון נופל על יולדת:
rashi.eng: *Be in pain.* Heb. חוּלִי, an expression of pain, as in (verse 9) “that pangs (חִיל) have seized you.” This expression is appropriate for a woman in confinement.

rashi.heb:
*וגוחי.* 
כרעי ושחי על גחונך וכן בלשון משנה כותל הגוחה לרשות הרבים:
rashi.eng: *and kneel.* Heb. וָגֹחִי, kneel and bend down on your belly (גָחוֹן). So it is in the language of the Mishnah (Moed Katan 7a): “A wall that bends over (הַגוֹחֶה) into a public domain.”

rashi.heb:
*תצאי מקריה.* 
מירושלים ללכת בגולה:
rashi.eng: *you shall go forth from the city.* From Jerusalem, to go into exile.

rashi.heb:
*ושכנת בשדה.* 
תהי שכינתך חרושה כשדה:
rashi.eng: *and you shall dwell in the field.* Your dwelling shall be plowed up like a field.

notes.189: (tn, Heb): “let her be desecrated.” the referent (Jerusalem) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.190: (tn, Heb): “and let our eye look upon Zion.”

rashi.heb:
*האומרים תחנף.* 
עתה תתחייב ציון בחטאתיה ויפקד עליה עוונה:
rashi.eng: *who say, “Let her be guilty”.* Let Zion be guilty of her sins, and let her iniquity be visited upon her.

rashi.heb:
*ותחז בציון עינינו.* 
ותראינה בה עינינו מה שאוינו לראות בה:
rashi.eng: *and our eyes shall gaze on Zion.* And our eyes will see in her what we hoped to see her.

notes.191: (tn): The words “to be threshed” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation to make it clear that the Lord is planning to enable “Daughter Zion” to “thresh” her enemies.

rashi.heb:
*כי קבצם כעמיר גורנה.* 
וסופו לקבצם אל עמק יהושפט וסביבו' ירושלים למלחמ' כמו שמקבצין עמיר כדי לדושם שם אף הם חיל גוג ומגוג לרעתם נאספו ויאמר הקב"ה לכנ"י קומי ודושי בת ציון:
rashi.eng: *for He gathered them as sheaves to a threshing floor.* And eventually, He will gather them to the Valley of Jehoshaphat and around Jerusalem to war, as they gather a sheaf in order to thresh it there. The heathens, too, will be gathered there for their detriment, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to the people of Israel: “Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion.”

notes.192: (tn, Heb): “I will make your horn iron.”
notes.193: (sn): Jerusalem (Daughter Zion at the beginning of the verse; cf. 4:8) is here compared to a powerful ox which crushes the grain on the threshing floor with its hooves.
notes.194: (tn, Heb): Or “the Lord” (so many English versions); “the master.”
notes.195: (tn, Heb): “and their wealth to the master of all the earth.” The verb “devote” does double duty in the parallelism and is supplied in the second line for clarification. In vv. 11-13 the prophet jumps from the present crisis (which will result in exile, v. 10) to a time beyond the restoration of the exiles when God will protect his city from invaders. The Lord’s victory over the Assyrian armies in 701 b.c. foreshadowed this.

rashi.heb:
*והחרמתי.* 
לשון הקדש:
rashi.eng: *and I will devote.* Heb. וְהַחֲרַמְתִּי, an expression of hallowing.

rashi.heb:
*בצעם.* 
מה שכנסו מגזילה וחמס:
rashi.eng: *their plunder.* What they gathered from robbery and violence.

rashi.heb:
*וחילם.* 
ונכסיהון:
rashi.eng: *and their wealth.* Their possessions.

rashi.heb:
*עתה תתגודדי בת גדוד.* 
עתה בעת גזרתה הרעה על העון כי גבר תתגודדי בת גדוד בת כשדים קבצי גדודין כי עתה הוא אשר תצלחי בגדוד אשר שם מצור עלינו:
rashi.eng: *Now you shall gather yourself in troops, O daughter of troops.* Now, at the time of its [Israel’s] evil decree concerning the iniquity, which has increased, you shall gather yourself in troops, O daughter of troops; O daughter of the Chaldeans, gather troops, for now you shall succeed with the troop that laid siege upon us.

rashi.heb:
*בשבט יכו על הלחי.* 
מי גרם לך להצליח את אשר ישראל מלעיבי' על נביאיהם ושופטיה' ומכים אותם על הלחי כך היו עושים וכן מצינו בפסיקתא וכן ישעיה הוא אומר (ישעיהו נ׳:ו׳) גוי נתתי למכים:
rashi.eng: *With a rod, they strike… on the cheek.* Who caused them (Babylon) to succeed? The Israelites deride their prophets and their judges and strike them on the cheek. So were they wont to do, and so we find in Pesikta (d’Rav Kahana, p. 125b), and so does Isaiah say, (Isa. 50:6) “I gave my back to smiters.”

notes.196: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ by one from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with ET = HT, ET = HT, ET = HT, etc., through ET = HT. From the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Hebrew Bible are again the same.
notes.197: (tn): The Hebrew verb גָדַד (gadad) can be translated “slash yourself” or “gather in troops.” A number of English translations are based on the latter meaning (e.g., NASB, NIV, NLT). Slash yourself. Slashing one’s body was a form of mourning. See Deut 14:1; 1 Kgs 18:28; Jer 16:6; 41:5; 47:5.
notes.198: (tn, Heb): “daughter of a troop of warriors.” The daughter surrounded by soldiers is an image of the city of Jerusalem under siege (note the address “Daughter Jerusalem” in 4:8).
notes.199: (tn): Or “staff”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT “rod”; CEV “stick”; NCV “club.” Striking a king with a scepter, a symbol of rulership, would be especially ironic and humiliating.
notes.200: (tn): Traditionally, “the judge of Israel” (so KJV, NASB).

rashi.heb:
*ואתה בית לחם אפרתה.* 
שיצא דוד משם שנאמר בו (שמואל א י״ז:נ״ח) עבדך ישי בית הלחמי ובית לחם קרוי אפרת שנאמר (בראשית מ״ח:ז׳) בדרך אפרת היא בית לחם:
rashi.eng: *And you, Bethlehem Ephrathah.* whence David emanated, as it is stated (I Sam. 17:58): “The son of your bondsman, Jesse the Bethlehemite.” And Bethlehem is called Ephrath, as it is said (Gen. 48:7): “On the road to Ephrath, that is Bethlehem.”

rashi.heb:
*צעיר להיות באלפי יהודה.* 
ראוי היית להיות צעיר במשפחות יהודה מפני פסולת רות המואביה שבך:
rashi.eng: *you should have been the lowest of the clans of Judah.* You should have been the lowest of the clans of Judah because of the stigma of Ruth the Moabitess in you.

rashi.heb:
*ממך לי יצא.* 
משיח בן דוד וכה"א (תהילים קי״ח:כ״ב) אבן מאסו הבונים:
rashi.eng: *from you shall emerge for Me.* the Messiah, son of David, and so Scripture says (Ps. 118:22): “The stone the builders had rejected became a cornerstone.”

rashi.heb:
*ומוצאותיו מקדם.* 
לפני שמש ינון שמו (שם):
rashi.eng: *and his origin is from of old.* “Before the sun his name is Yinnon” (Ps. 72:17).

notes.201: (sn): Ephrathah is either an alternate name for Bethlehem or the name of the district in which Bethlehem was located. See Ruth 4:11. For location of Bethlehem see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
notes.202: (tn, Heb): “being small.” Some omit לִהְיוֹת (lihyot, “being”) because it fits awkwardly and appears again in the next line.
notes.203: (tn, Heb): “from you for me one will go out to be a ruler over Israel.”
notes.204: (tn, Heb): “his goings out.” The term may refer to the ruler’s origins (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT) or to his activities.
notes.205: (tn, Heb): “from the past, from the days of antiquity.” Elsewhere both phrases refer to the early periods in the history of the world or of the nation of Israel. For מִקֶּדֶם (miqqedem, “from the past”) see Neh 12:46; Pss 74:12; 77:11; Isa 45:21; 46:10. For מִימֵי עוֹלָם (mimey ’olam, “from the days of antiquity”) see Isa 63:9, 11; Amos 9:11; Mic 7:14; Mal 3:4. In Neh 12:46 and Amos 9:11 the Davidic era is in view. In riddle-like fashion this verse alludes to David, as the references to Bethlehem and to his ancient origins/activities indicate. The passage anticipates the second coming of the great king to usher in a new era of national glory for Israel. Other prophets are more direct and name this coming ideal ruler “David” (Jer 30:9; Ezek 34:23-24; 37:24-25; Hos 3:5). Of course, this prophecy of “David’s” second coming is actually fulfilled through his descendant, the Messiah, who will rule in the spirit and power of his famous ancestor and bring to realization the Davidic royal ideal in an even greater way than the historical David (see Isa 11:1, 10; Jer 33:15).

rashi.heb:
*לכן יתנם עד עת יולדה.* 
יתנם ביד אויביהם עד בא העת אשר חלה וילדה ציון את בניה ציון אשר החזיקה עתה חיל כיולדה ועכשיו היא קרויה יולדת ורבותינו אמרו מכאן אין בן דוד בא עד שתפשוט המלכות הרשעה ט' חדשים על כל העולם כולו אך לפי פשוטו זהו הצעה שפירשתי:
rashi.eng: *Therefore, He shall deliver them until the time a woman in confinement gives birth.* He shall deliver them into the hands of their enemies until the coming of the time that Zion has felt the pangs of labor and borne her children; Zion, which is now seized by the pangs of labor, is now called a woman in confinement. [I.e., now the labor pains will cease and the redemption will come about.] But our Sages state that from here we deduce that the son of David will not come until the wicked kingdom spreads over the entire world for nine months (Yoma 10b, Sanh. 98b). But, according to its simple meaning, this is the structure as I explained.

rashi.heb:
*ויתר אחיו.* 
של מלך יהודה כלומר שאר שבט יהודה:
rashi.eng: *and the rest of his brothers.* The brothers of the King Messiah; i. e., the rest of the tribe [of Judah].

rashi.heb:
*ישובון על בית ישראל.* 
יתחברו עם שאר השבטי' והיו לממלכה אחת ולא יחצו עוד לשתי ממלכות:
rashi.eng: *shall return upon the children of Israel.* Judah and Benjamin shall join the other tribes and become one kingdom, and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

notes.206: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.207: (tn, Heb): “them”; the referent (the people of Israel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.208: (tn): The words “to their enemies” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.209: (sn): The woman in labor. Personified, suffering Jerusalem is the referent. See 4:9-10.
notes.210: (sn): Gives birth. The point of the figurative language is that Jerusalem finally finds relief from her suffering. See 4:10.
notes.211: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.212: (tn, Heb): “to the sons of Israel.” The words “be reunited with” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The rest of the king’s brothers are the coming king’s fellow Judahites, while the sons of Israel are the northern tribes. The verse pictures the reunification of the nation under the Davidic king. See Isa 11:12-13; Jer 31:2-6, 15-20; Ezek 37; Hos 1:11; 3:5.

rashi.heb:
*ורעה.* 
ופרנס את ישראל:
rashi.eng: *and lead.* Heb. וְרָעָה. And lead (וּפִרְנֵס) Israel.

rashi.heb:
*וישובו.* 
מן הגליות:
rashi.eng: *and they shall return.* Heb. וְיָשָׁבוּ. They shall return now from the exiles.

rashi.heb:
*כי עתה יגדל.* 
מלכם:
rashi.eng: *for then he shall become great.* I.e., their king.

rashi.heb:
*עד אפסי ארץ.* 
והביאום מנחה אליו בסוסים וברכב:
rashi.eng: *until the ends of the earth.* And they shall bring tribute to him [the Messiah] with horses and chariots.

notes.213: (tn, Heb): “stand up”; NAB “stand firm”; NASB “will arise.”
notes.214: (tn): The words “the people” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.215: (tn, Heb): “by the majesty of the name of the Lord his God.”
notes.216: (tn): The words “in peace” are supplied in the translation for clarification. Perhaps וְיָשָׁבוּ (v�yashavu, “and they will live”) should be emended to וְשָׁבוּ (v�shavu, “and they will return”).

rashi.heb:
*והיה זה שלום.* 
גמור וקבוע באין הפסק עוד ולא ידמה לשאר התשועות שהיו צרות אחריהן:
rashi.eng: *And this shall be peace.* A complete and permanent peace, without interruption, and it will not resemble the other redemptions after which there were troubles.

rashi.heb:
*אשור כי יבא.* 
הרי כי משמש בלשון אם, אם יבא בארצנו כאשר בא עתה:
rashi.eng: *should Assyria come.* Heb כִּי יָבוֹא. This כִּי serves as “if” - If he comes into our land as he comes now.

rashi.heb:
*והקימונו עליו שבעה רועים.* 
שבעה ושמונה רבותינו פירשו שמותיהן במסכת סוכה ואיני יודע מהיכן למדו:
rashi.eng: *we will appoint over them seven shepherds and eight.* Concerning the seven and eight, our Rabbis enumerated their names in Tractate Sukkah, but I do not know whence they derived them. [referring to Sukkah 52b]

notes.219: (tn, Heb): “and this one will be peace”; ASV “and this man shall be our peace” (cf. Eph 2:14).
notes.220: (tc): Some prefer to read “in our land,” emending the text to בְּאַדְמָתֵנוּ (b�’admatenu).
notes.222: (sn): The numbers seven and eight here symbolize completeness and emphasize that Israel will have more than enough military leadership and strength to withstand the Assyrian advance.

rashi.heb:
*ורעו את ארץ אשור.* 
וירוצצו כמו (שם ב) תרועם בשבט ברזל:
rashi.eng: *And they shall break the land of Assyria.* Heb. יְרָעוּ. And they shall break, similar to (Ps. 2:9) “You shall break them (תְּרֹעֵם) with an iron rod.”

rashi.heb:
*ואת ארץ נמרוד.* 
היא בבל:
rashi.eng: *and the land of Nimrod.* That is Babylon.

rashi.heb:
*בפתחיה.* 
בשערי מדינותיה:
rashi.eng: *at its gates.* Heb. בִּפְתָחֶיה, at the gates of its provinces.

notes.226: (sn): According to Gen 10:8-12, Nimrod, who was famous as a warrior and hunter, founded Assyria.
notes.227: (tc): The MT reads “in her gates,” but the text should be emended to בַּפְּתִיחָה (baptikhah, “with a drawn sword”).
notes.228: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the coming king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*כטל מאת ה'.* 
שאין בא לעולם ע"י אדם ולא יבקשו פני אדם עליו כך לא יקוה ישראל לעזרת איש כי אם בה':
rashi.eng: *like dew sent by the Lord.* which does not come to the world through man, and people do not ask for it, so Israel will not hope for the help of man, but for the Lord.

notes.231: (tn): This could mean “(scattered) among the nations” (cf. CEV, NLT) or “surrounded by many nations” (cf. NRSV).
notes.232: (tn, Heb): “that does not hope for man, and does not wait for the sons of men.” Men wait eagerly for the dew and the rain, not vice versa. Just as the dew and rain are subject to the Lord, not men, so the remnant of Israel will succeed by the supernatural power of God and not need the support of other nations. There may even be a military metaphor here. Israel will overwhelm their enemies, just as the dew completely covers the grass (see 2 Sam 17:12). This interpretation would be consistent with the image of v. 7.

rashi.heb:
*כאריה בבהמות יער.* 
כך יהי מלכם שליט בכל:
rashi.eng: *like a lion among the beasts of the forest.* So will their king rule over all.

rashi.heb:
*ורמס וטרף.* 
רמס היא דריסת הארי כשהוא רעב ואוכלו במקומו וטרף הוא כשנושא את הטרף למעונותיו בשביל גורותיו ולבאותיו:
rashi.eng: *which treads down and tears in pieces.* Heb. רָמַס. This is the lion’s treading down [an animal] when he [the lion] is hungry and eating it in its place. Tearing (טָרַף) is when he carries the prey to his den for his cubs and his lionesses.

notes.233: (tn): The words “its prey” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

notes.235: (tn, Heb): “let your hand be lifted against your adversaries.”

rashi.heb:
*והכרתי סוסיך.* 
היא עזרת מצרים שאתם נשענים עליהם להמציאכם סוסים:
rashi.eng: *that I will cut your horses.* the Egyptian aid upon which you rely to supply you with horses.

notes.237: (tn, Heb): “cut off” (also in the following verse).

rashi.heb:
*והכרתי ערי ארצך.* 
ולא תצטרך לערי מבצר:
rashi.eng: *And I will destroy your cities.* And you will no longer need fortified cities.

notes.238: (tn, Heb): “magic charms” (so NCV, TEV); NIV, NLT “witchcraft”; NAB “the means of divination.” The precise meaning of this Hebrew word is uncertain, but note its use in Isa 47:9, 12.
notes.240: (tn, Heb): “and you will not have omen-readers.”

rashi.heb:
*והשמדתי עריך.* 
ואשיצי בעלי דבבך וכן (ישעיהו י״ד:כ״א) ומלאו פני תבל ערים וכן (שמואל א כח) ויהי עריך:
rashi.eng: *and I will destroy your enemies.* Heb. עָרֶיךָ. Jonathan renders: And I will destroy your enemies. Similarly, (Isa. 14:21) “And fill the surface of the earth with enemies (עָרִים) ,” and (I Sam. 28:16) “And has become your adversary (עָרֶךָ).”

notes.241: (tn): Or “Asherah poles.” Asherah was a leading deity of the Canaanite pantheon, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. She was commonly worshiped at shrines in or near groves of evergreen trees, or, failing that, at places marked by wooden poles. These were to be burned or cut down (Deut 12:3; 16:21; Judg 6:25, 28, 30; 2 Kgs 18:4). The Lord states that he will destroy these images, something the Israelites themselves should have done but failed to do.
notes.242: (tn): The MT reads “your cities,” but many emend the text to צִרֶיךָ (tsirekha, “your images”) or עֲצַבֶּיךָ (’atsbbekha, “your idols”).

notes.243: (tn, Heb): “I will accomplish in anger and in rage, vengeance on the nations who do not listen.”

notes.244: (tn): Or “plead your case” (NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “present your plea”; NLT “state your case.” Defend yourself. The Lord challenges Israel to defend itself against the charges he is bringing.
notes.245: (sn): As in some ancient Near Eastern treaties, the mountains are personified as legal witnesses that will settle the dispute between God and Israel.
notes.246: (tn, Heb): “let the hills hear your voice.”

rashi.heb:
*את ההרים.* 
את האבות:
rashi.eng: *with the mountains.* with the Patriarchs.

rashi.heb:
*הגבעות.* 
האמהות:
rashi.eng: *the hills.* the Matriarchs.

notes.247: (tn): This verse briefly interrupts the Lord’s statement (see vv. 1, 3) as the prophet summons the mountains as witnesses. Because of this v. 2 has been placed in parentheses in the translation.

notes.248: (tn, Heb): “My people, what have I done to you?”

rashi.heb:
*מה עשיתי לך.* 
תן לבך להכיר מה טוב עשיתי לך:
rashi.eng: *what have I done for you.* Put your heart to recognizing what benefit I have done for you.

rashi.heb:
*ומה הלאתיך.* 
בעבודתי:
rashi.eng: *and how have I wearied you.* with My worship?

rashi.heb:
*ענה בי.* 
העד בי:
rashi.eng: *Testify against Me.* Heb. ענה בי: Testify against me.

rashi.heb:
*כי העליתיך.* 
אע"פ שעשיתי לך כל הטובה הזאת לא הלאתיך בעבודה גדולה ובקרבנות גדולים:
rashi.eng: *For I brought you up.* Although I bestowed all this benefit upon you, I did not weary you with much worship or with large sacrifices.

rashi.heb:
*את משה אהרן ומרים.* 
ת"י משה לאלפא מסורת דינין ואהרן לכפרא על עמא ומרים לאוראה לנשיא:
rashi.eng: *Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.* Jonathan paraphrases: Moses to teach the transmission of the laws, Aaron to atone for the people, and Miriam to instruct the women.

notes.251: (tn, Heb): “From Shittim to Gilgal, in order to know the just acts of the Lord.” Something appears to be missing at the beginning of the line. The present translation supplies the words, “Recall how you went.” This apparently refers to how Israel crossed the Jordan River (see Josh 3:1; 4:19-24).

rashi.heb:
*ומה ענה אותו בלעם בן בעור.* 
מה אזעום לא זעם ה' (במדבר כ״ג:ח׳) שלא כעסתי כל אותן הימים:
rashi.eng: *and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him.* (Num. 23:8) “How shall I be angry if God is not angry?” For I did not become angry all those days. [from Berachot 7a]

rashi.heb:
*מן השטים.* 
שחטאתם לי שם דעו צדקותי שלא מנעתי טובתי ועזרתי מכם עד הבאתי אתכם לגלגל וכבשתי לפניכם שם את הארץ:
rashi.eng: *from Shittim.* where you sinned before Me. You should recognize My righteous deeds, for I did not withhold My kindness and My assistance from you until I brought you to Gilgal, and I conquered the land before you.

notes.252: (sn): With what should I enter the Lord’s presence? The prophet speaks again, playing the role of an inquisitive worshiper who wants to know what God really desires from his followers.
notes.253: (tn): The words “with what” do double duty in the parallelism and are supplied in the second line of the translation for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*אכף.* 
אהיה כפוף:
rashi.eng: *bow.* I will be humbled.

notes.255: (tn, Heb): “the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) is often translated “soul,” but the word usually refers to the whole person; here “the sin of my soul” = “my sin.”

rashi.heb:
*נחלי שמן.* 
למנחות:
rashi.eng: *streams of oil.* for meal offerings.

rashi.heb:
*האתן בכורי.* 
קרבן לפשעי:
rashi.eng: *Shall I give my firstborn?.* as a sacrifice for my transgression.

notes.256: (sn): What the Lord really wants from you. Now the prophet switches roles and answers the hypothetical worshiper’s question. He makes it clear that the Lord desires proper attitudes more than ritual and sacrifice.
notes.257: (tn, Heb): “except.” This statement is actually linked with what precedes, “What does he want from you except….”
notes.258: (tn, Heb): “to do,” in the sense of “promote.”

rashi.heb:
*הגיד.* 
הקב"ה לך אדם מה טוב לך לעשות:
rashi.eng: *He has told.* The Holy One, blessed be He, has told you what is good for you to do.

rashi.heb:
*והצנע לכת.* 
ת"י הוי צנוע למיהך בדחלא דאלהך, ד"א והצנע לכת לא כמדת הקב"ה מדת בשר ודם מדת בשר ודם אדם מבייש את חבירו ובא לפייסו ואומר לו איני מתרצה לך עד שיבא פלוני ופלוני שבזיתני לפניהם אבל הקב"ה אין חפץ אלא שישוב אליו בינו לבין עצמו:
rashi.eng: *and to walk discreetly.* Jonathan renders: Walk discreetly in the fear of your God. Another explanation: And walk discreetly. The standard of flesh and blood is not like the standard of the Holy One, blessed be He. The standard of flesh and blood is: If one man embarrasses his fellow and comes to placate him, the fellow says to him, “I will not accept your apology until so and so and so and so, before whom you disgraced me, come.” But the Holy One, blessed be He, desires only that the man’s return to Him be between the two of them. [from Pesikta d’Rav Kahana 163b]

notes.261: (tn): Or “the voice of the Lord is calling.” The translation understands קוֹל (qol, “voice”) as equivalent to an imperative.
notes.262: (tn, Heb): “one who sees your name is wisdom.” It is probably better to emend יִרְאֶה (yir’eh, “he sees”) to יִרְאָה (yir’ah, “fearing”). One may then translate, “fearing your name is wisdom.” The Lord’s “name” here stands by metonymy for his authority.
notes.263: (tn, Heb): (apparently) “Listen [to] the staff and the one who appointed it.” Verse 10 then begins with עוֹד (yod, “still” or “again”). The translation assumes an emendation to שִׁמְעוּ מַטֶּה וּמוֹעֵד הָעִיר (shim’u matteh umo’ed ha’ir, “listen, O tribe and the assembly of the city”).

rashi.heb:
*קול ה' לעיר יקרא.* 
קל נבייא דה' על קרתא מכריזין להם תשובה:
rashi.eng: *The voice of the Lord calls out in the city.* The voice of the prophets of the Lord calling out, calling them [the people] to repentance. [from Jonathan]

rashi.heb:
*ותושיה יראה שמך.* 
ותושיה קורא להם הנביא אשר רואה את שמך אשר נותן לב להתבונן ולראות דרכיך ותושיה מוסב על מקרא שלמעלה הימנו:
rashi.eng: *and the wisdom of the Torah, the one who sees Your name.* The prophet who sees Your name calls out the wisdom of the Torah; i.e., the one who puts his heart to contemplate and to see your ways. The word וְתוּשִׁיּה refers to the verse above it.

rashi.heb:
*שמעו מטה ומי יעדה.* 
הטו אזן ושמעו מטה הפורענות אשר תרדה אתכם שהנביאים מתרים בכם ושמעו מי הוא אשר ייעד אותו הפורענות אם יכולת בידו לקיים מה שגוזר ויונתן לא כן תירגם:
rashi.eng: *hearken to the staff and Who appointed it.* Bend your ears, and hearken to the staff of retribution that will punish you, concerning which the prophets warn you; and hearken to who it is Who appointed that retribution, whether He has the ability to fulfill what He decreed. But Jonathan did not render in this manner.

rashi.heb:
*ותושיה יראה שמך.* 
מכאן שכל מי שאומר בכל יום מקרא המתחיל ומסיים כמו שמתחיל ומסיים שמו התורה מצילו מגיהנם):
rashi.eng: *and the wisdom of Torah, the one who sees Your name.* From here we deduce that whoever recites daily a verse beginning [with the letter] and ending [with the letter] as his name begins and ends, the Torah saves him from Gehinnom.

notes.264: (tn): The meaning of the first Hebrew word in the line is unclear. Possibly it is a combination of the interrogative particle and אִשׁ (’ish), an alternate form of יֵשׁ (yesh, “there is/are”). One could then translate literally, “Are there treasures of sin [in] the house of the sinful?” The translation assumes an emendation to הַאֶשֶּׁה (ha’esheh, from נָשָׁא, nasha’, “to forget”), “Will I forget?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “No, I will not forget.”
notes.265: (tn, Heb): “the treasures of sin”; NASB “treasures of wickedness”; NIV “ill-gotten treasures.”
notes.266: (tn, Heb): “the accursed scant measure.” Merchants would use a smaller than standard measure so they could give the customer less than he thought he was paying for.

rashi.heb:
*עוד האש בית רשע אוצרות רשע.*
