ה"א האש נקודה פתח לפי שהיא תמוה וכן פירושו עוד ל' אורך ימים הוא, האש כמו היש (ובד"ה א ב) מצינו אישי אבי דוד במקום ישי אף כאן אש במקום יש וכן (בשמואל ב י״ד:י״ט) אם אש להמין ולהשמאיל אם יש להאמין ולהשמאיל, וי"ת כן האית שיעלה בלבבכם שיתקיים בית רשע לאורך ימי' ואוצרות רשע:
rashi.eng: *Does the house of the wicked last long, [or do] the treasures of wickedness?.* The “hey” of הַאִשׁ is vowelized with a “pattach” [not a kamatz] because it denotes a question. And this is its meaning: עוֹד is an expression of longevity. הַאִשׁ is like הֲיֵשׁ, is there. In I Chronicles (2:13) we find: “Ishai the father of David,” instead of “Yishai.” Here, too, is אִשׁ instead of יֵשׁ. And so in II Samuel (14:19): “If anyone can (אִשׁ) turn to the right or to the left.” [This is identical to] “If anyone can (יֵשׁ) turn to the right or to the left.” So did Jonathan render it: Is there. Will it enter your mind that the house of the wicked will last long, and the treasures of wickedness?

rashi.heb:
*ואיפת רזון זעומה.* 
מדה קטנה שעשיריכם מרמים בה העניים ומביאין אותן לידי רזון והוא זעומה באפו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *And an ephah of leanness is condemned.* A small measure with which your wealthy deceive the poor and bring them to leanness - that is condemned by the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He.

notes.267: (tn, Heb): “Do I acquit sinful scales, and a bag of deceptive weights?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “No, I do not,” and has been translated as a declarative statement for clarity and emphasis. Merchants also used rigged scales and deceptive weights to cheat their customers. See the note at Amos 8:5.

notes.268: (tn, Heb): “because her rich are full of violence.”
notes.270: (tn, Heb): “and their tongue is deceptive in their mouth.”

notes.271: (tn, Heb): “and also I, I will make you sick, striking you.”

rashi.heb:
*החליתי הכותך.* 
האנשתי מכותיך חזקות וחולות ואנושו':
rashi.eng: *I will smite you with sore wounds.* I have made your wounds sore - strong and ill and incurable.

rashi.heb:
*השמם.* 
להשמימך על חטאתיך:
rashi.eng: *and make [you] desolate.* Heb. הַשְׁמֵם, to make you desolate because of your sins.

notes.272: (tc): The first Hebrew term in the line (וְיֶשְׁחֲךָ, v�yeshkhakha) is obscure. HALOT 446 s.v. יֶשַׁח understands a noun meaning “filth,” which would yield the translation, “and your filth is inside you.” The translation assumes an emendation to כֹּחַ-וְיֶשׁ (v�yesh-koakh, “and [if] there is strength inside you”).
notes.273: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew term וְתַסֵּג (v�tasseg) is unclear. The translation assumes it is a Hiphal imperfect from נָסַג/נָשַׂג (nasag/nasag, “reach; overtake”) and that hunting imagery is employed. (Note the reference to hunger in the first line of the verse.) See D. R. Hillers, Micah (Hermeneia), 80.
notes.274: (tn): The Hiphal of פָּלַט (palat) is used in Isa 5:29 of an animal carrying its prey to a secure place.

rashi.heb:
*וישחך בקרבך.* 
המאכל שתאכל אכניס בו מארה בתוך המעים ויגרום לך חולי שתהא חולה והולך שחוח וכן מפרש אותו בספרי מניין אף בתוך המעים ת"ל וישחך בקרבך בפרשת והיה עקב במדרש תמיד עיני ה' אלהיך בה ואף יונתן תירגם כן ויהי לך למרע מתא במעיך:
rashi.eng: *and it shall bend you over in your innards.* Heb. וְיֶשְׁחֲךָ. The food that you eat - I will bring a curse into it within your intestines, and it will cause you illness, that you will be ill and walk bent over. So it is explained in Sifre: How do we know that, even within the intestines? Scripture states: “And it shall bend you over in your innards.” In the parashah of Ekev, in expounding (Deut. 11:12) “The eyes of the Lord your God are upon it,” Jonathan, too, renders [our verse] in this manner: And it shall be to you for illness and a wound in your intestines.

rashi.heb:
*ותסג.* 
את אויביך המוליכים בניך ובנותיך בשבי ולא תפלטם ואם תפלטם סופם לחרב ומשמו של ר' מנחם שמעתי ותסג לתאות תשמיש ולא תפליט לא יהי' לך כח לפלוט שכבת זרע ואם תפלטם סופה לחרב אתן אתכם וי"ת ל' הראשון:
rashi.eng: *and you shall overtake.* your enemies who lead your sons and daughters away, into captivity; but you shall not rescue them, and if you rescue them, their end will be to the sword. In the name of Rabbi Menahem I heard: You shall gain your desire for sexual intercourse, but you shall not ejaculate. You shall not have the strength to ejaculate semen; and, if you do ejaculate them [and beget children], their end will be that I will deliver them to the sword [of the enemy].

notes.275: (tn, Heb): “you will tread olives.” Literally treading on olives with one’s feet could be harmful and would not supply the necessary pressure to release the oil. See O. Borowski, Agriculture in Iron Age Israel, 119. The Hebrew term דָּרַךְ (darakh) may have an idiomatic sense of “press” here, or perhaps the imagery of the following parallel line (referring to treading grapes) has dictated the word choice.
notes.276: (tn, Heb): “but you will not rub yourselves with oil.”
notes.277: (tn, Heb): “and juice, but you will not drink wine.” The verb תִדְרֹךְ (tidrokh, “you will tread”) must be supplied from the preceding line.

notes.278: (tn, Heb): “the edicts of Omri are kept, and all the deeds of the house of Ahab.”
notes.279: (tn, Heb): “and you walk in their plans.” The Omride dynasty, of which Ahab was the most infamous king, had a reputation for implementing unjust and oppressive measures. See 1 Kgs 21.
notes.280: (tn): The Hebrew term שַׁמָּה (shammah) can refer to “destruction; ruin,” or to the reaction it produces in those who witness the destruction.
notes.281: (tn, Heb): “her”; the referent (the city) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.282: (tn, Heb): “[an object] of hissing,” which was a way of taunting someone.
notes.283: (tc, Heb): The translation assumes an emendation of the MT’s עַמִּי (’ammi, “my people”) to עַמִּים (’ammim, “nations”). “and the reproach of my people you will bear.” The second person verb is plural here, in contrast to the singular forms used in vv. 13-15.

rashi.heb:
*וישתמר חוקות עמרי.* 
וידעתי כי לא תשמעו אלי כי ישתמר על ידיכם וביניכם כל חוקות עמרי ואחאב:
rashi.eng: *And the statutes of Omri shall be observed.* I know that you will not obey Me, but through you and your children will all the statutes of Omri and Ahab [the evil kings of Israel] be observed.

rashi.heb:
*וחרפת עמי תשאו.* 
אתם תקבלון עון החרפה שהעכו"ם מחרפין את עמי שהעידה בהם תורה על כך (דברים כ״ה:י״ד) לא יהיה לך איפ' ואיפה והם אינם שומרים:
rashi.eng: *and the disgrace of My people you shall bear.* You shall bear the iniquity for the disgrace that the peoples of the world deride My people, for the Torah admonished them concerning (Deut. 25:14): “You shall not have in your house two kinds of ephah,” but they do not keep it.

notes.284: (tn, Heb): “woe to me!” In light of the image that follows, perhaps one could translate, “I am disappointed.”
notes.286: (tn, Heb): “I am like the gathering of the summer fruit, like the gleanings of the harvest.” Micah is not comparing himself to the harvested fruit. There is an ellipsis here, as the second half of the verse makes clear. The idea is, “I am like [one at the time] the summer fruit is gathered and the grapes are harvested.”

rashi.heb:
*אללי לי.* 
הנביא מקונן על עצמו אוי לי שהועמדתי לנביא בעת הזאת שאין בנ"א צדיקים בדור:
rashi.eng: *Woe is to me.* The prophet laments over himself, “Woe is to me that I was appointed a prophet at this time, when there are no righteous people in the generation.”

rashi.heb:
*כאספי קיץ.* 
נקוד חטף קמץ שאינו ל' פועל כמו יושב אומר אלא לשון מפעל כמו (ישעיהו ל״ג:ד׳) אוסף החסיל כאסיפת קיץ והם סופי תאינים שהן רעות וכן תרגם יונתן כסיופי קייטא:
rashi.eng: *as the last of the figs.* Heb. כְּאָסְפֵּי. This is vowelized with a “chataf kamatz” because it is not a verb in the present tense, like:, יוֹשֵב, sits, and אוֹמֵר, says; rather, it is a gerund, as in (Isa. 33:4): “The gathering of (אֹסֶף) the locusts”; like the gathering of קַיִץ. These are the last figs, which are inferior. And so did Jonathan render: as the late figs of the summer.

rashi.heb:
*כעוללות בציר.* 
ת"י כעוללן בתר קטוף:
rashi.eng: *as the gleanings of the vintage.* As the gleanings after the vintage. [from Jonathan]

rashi.heb:
*אין אשכול לאכול.* 
כתרגומו לית גבר דביה עובדין טבין:
rashi.eng: *there is no cluster to eat.* As the Targum renders: There is no man who has good deeds.

rashi.heb:
*בכורה.* 
תאינה טובה המתבשלת בעתה כתרגומו לטביא חמדת נפשי:
rashi.eng: *a first ripe fig my soul desires.* A good fig, which ripens in its time, as the Targum renders: My soul desired the good ones.

notes.289: (tn, Heb): “and an upright one among men there is not.”
notes.290: (tn, Heb): “for bloodshed” (so NASB); TEV “for a chance to commit murder.”
notes.291: (sn): Micah compares these ungodly people to hunters trying to capture their prey with a net.

rashi.heb:
*וישר באדם אין.* 
אדם ישר בבני אדם אין:
rashi.eng: *and there is no upright among men.* There is no upright man among men.

rashi.heb:
*יצודו חרם.* 
יצודו בחרמם ובמצודתם:
rashi.eng: *each one hunts his brother with a net.* They hunt with their net and with their trap.

notes.292: (tn, Heb): “upon evil [are their] hands to do [it] well.”
notes.293: (tn, Heb): “the official asks – and the judge – for a bribe.”
notes.294: (tn): More literally, “the great one announces what his appetite desires and they weave it together.” Apparently this means that subordinates plot and maneuver to make sure the prominent man’s desires materialize.

rashi.heb:
*על הרע כפים להטיב.* 
על שכר הרעת כפיכם אתם מקוים שיטיב לכם:
rashi.eng: *[in return] for the evil of their hands, do they expect that He will benefit them?.* Do you expect that He will benefit you as the reward for the evil of your hands?

rashi.heb:
*השר שואל.* 
שוחד:
rashi.eng: *the prince asks.* for a bribe.

rashi.heb:
*והשופט.* 
הדן את הדין גם הוא בשילום אומר לשופט חבירו כשהוא גזלן ומחויב בדין שלם לי גמולי בזה ואני אזכה אותך בדין אחר:
rashi.eng: *and the judge.* who judges the case is also in the payment. When he is a robber and is liable according to law, he says to his fellow judge, “Do me a favor in this case, and I will vindicate you in another case.”

rashi.heb:
*והגדול דובר הות נפשו.* 
המלך או הנשיא אומר בדין רצון נפשו:
rashi.eng: *and the great man speaks what is in his heart.* The king or the prince states in the case what his heart desires.

rashi.heb:
*הות נפשו.* 
דבר ההוה לרצונו. ולנפשו כמו (ירמיה טו) אין נפשי אל העם הזה וכן ת"י תחמודי נפשיה:
rashi.eng: *what is in his heart.* Heb. הַוַּתנַפְשׁוֹ. He speaks what is (הוֹה) to his will and to his desire. Cf.(Jer. 15:1) “I have no desire for this people.” And so did Jonathan render: The desires of his heart.

rashi.heb:
*ויעבתוה.* 
עשאוה קליעה של חטא בין שלשתן כעבותות העגלה חטאה שהעבות משולשת היא כך מצאתי בתרגו' ירושלמי עבדנוה כקליעה דחובין:
rashi.eng: *and they weave the web.* They made it into a rope of sin amongst the three of them. As the cart ropes, so is the sin, for a rope is braided of three strands. So have I found in the Jerusalem Talmud (Taanith 2:1): We made it like a web of sins.

notes.295: (tn, Heb): “[the] godly from a row of thorn bushes.” The preposition מִן (min) is comparative and the comparative element (perhaps “sharper” is the idea) is omitted. See BDB 582 s.v. 6 and GKC 431 �133.e.
notes.296: (tn, Heb): “the day of your watchmen, your appointed [time], is coming.” The present translation takes “watchmen” to refer to actual sentries. However, the “watchmen” could refer figuratively to the prophets who had warned Judah of approaching judgment. In this case one could translate, “The day your prophets warned about – your appointed time of punishment – is on the way.”
notes.297: (tn, Heb): “and now will be their confusion.”

rashi.heb:
*טובם כחדק.* 
טבא דאית בהון קשה למיפק מן ידיה כד מן חדקא קשה לצאת מידו כמו הקוצים הנסבכין בצמר:
rashi.eng: *The best of them is like a brier.* The best among them - it is as hard to extricate oneself from his hand as from a brier (Targum Jonathan). It is as hard to extricate oneself from their hand as [it is to extricate] the briers that are entangled in wool.

rashi.heb:
*ישר ממסוכה.* 
ישר שבהם רע ממסוכת קוצים:
rashi.eng: *the most upright, [worse] than a thorn hedge.* The most upright among them is worse than a thorn hedge.

rashi.heb:
*מסוכה.* 
כמו (ישעיה ה) הסר מסוכתו:
rashi.eng: *than a thorn hedge.* Heb. מִמְּסוּכָה. Cf. (Isa. 5:5) “Remove its hedge (מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ).”

rashi.heb:
*יום מצפיך.* 
יום שאתה מצפה בו לטובה תבוא פקודתך:
rashi.eng: *the day to which you look forward.* On the day to which you look forward for good, your visitation shall come.

rashi.heb:
*מבוכתם.* 
עירבוליהון כמו (שמות יד) נבוכין הם מהומתם:
rashi.eng: *their perplexity.* Heb. מְבוּכָתָם. [Jonathan renders:] עֲרָבוּלָהוֹן. Cf. (Ex. 14:3) “They are entangled (נְבֻכִים).” Their confusion.

notes.298: (tn, Heb): “from the one who lies in your arms, guard the doors of your mouth.”

rashi.heb:
*אל תאמינו בריע.* 
כמשמעו ורבותינו פירשו כלפי מעלה אל תחטאו ותאמרו הקב"ה אוהבינו והוא ימחול לנו:
rashi.eng: *Believe not a friend.* [This is to be understood] according to its apparent meaning. But our Sages explained it as referring to the Most High. Do not sin and say that the Holy One, blessed be He, is our Friend, and He will forgive us. [from Hagiga 16a]

rashi.heb:
*משוכבת חיקך.* 
נשמתך היא תעיד בך:
rashi.eng: *from she who lies in your bosom.* Your soul will testify against you.

rashi.heb:
*פתחי פיך.* 
דברי פיך פתיחות פיך:
rashi.eng: *the openings of your mouth.* Heb. פִּתְחֵי. The words of your mouth, the openings of your mouth.

notes.300: (tn, Heb): “the enemies of a man are the men of his house.”

notes.301: (tn, Heb): “me.” In the interest of clarity the nature of the prophet’s cry has been specified as “my lament” in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*ואני בה' אצפה.* 
הנביא אומר כן:
rashi.eng: *But I will hope in the Lord.* The prophet is saying so.

notes.302: (tn): The singular form is understood as collective.
notes.303: (tn): Or “rejoice” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV); NCV “don’t laugh at me.”
notes.304: (sn): Darkness represents judgment; light (also in v. 9) symbolizes deliverance. The Lord is the source of the latter.

rashi.heb:
*אל תשמחי אויבתי.* 
בבל ועיר החייבת רומי (ס"א בבל ופרס החייבת):
rashi.eng: *Rejoice not… my enemy.* Babylon and the wicked city of Rome.

notes.307: (tn): Or “plead my case” (NASB and NIV both similar); NRSV “until he takes my side.”

notes.310: (tn, Heb): “who say.” A new sentence was begun here in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.311: (tn, Heb): “My eyes will look on them.”

notes.313: (sn): Personified Jerusalem declares her confidence in vv. 8-10; in this verse she is assured that she will indeed be vindicated.

rashi.heb:
*יום לבנות גדריך.* 
מוסב על האומרה אלי ועוד היא אומרת אלי יום לבנות גדריך שאת מצפה לו אותו היום:
rashi.eng: *“The day to build your walls”.* This refers back to “who says to me” : And she further says to me, “The day to build your walls, which you anticipate - that day…”

rashi.heb:
*ירחק חוקו.* 
זמנו יאריך ולא יבא לעולם:
rashi.eng: *“its time is way off”.* Heb. יִרְחַק-חֹק. Its time will be extended, and it will never come.

notes.314: (tn, Heb): “they.” The referent has been specified as “people,” referring either to the nations (coming to God with their tribute) or to the exiles of Israel (returning to the Lord).
notes.315: (tn): The masculine pronominal suffix suggests the Lord is addressed. Some emend to a feminine form and take Jerusalem as the addressee.
notes.316: (tc): The MT reads וְעָרֵי (v�’arey, “and the cities [of Egypt]”), but the parallel line indicates this is a corruption of וְעַד (v�’ad, “even to”).
notes.317: (tn, Heb): “the River,” referring to the Euphrates River. This has been specified in the translation for clarity (so also NASB, NIV).
notes.318: (tn, Heb): “and sea from sea.” Many prefer to emend this to מִיָּם עַד יָם (miyyam ’ad yam, “from sea to sea”).
notes.319: (tn, Heb): “and mountain of the mountain.” Many prefer to emend this to וּמֵהַר עַד הַר (umehar ’ad har, “and mountain to mountain”).

rashi.heb:
*יום הוא ועדיך יבא.* 
הנביא אומר אותו היום שאתם מלעיגים עליו לאמר בטל והלך לו יום ההוא שמור ונצור ולא בטל עדיך יבא בבל להחריבך:
rashi.eng: *It is a day, and he shall come up to you.* The prophet says: That day that you deride, saying that it has been nullified and gone away - that day is guarded and preserved, and has not become nullified. The enemy shall come up to you to destroy you.

rashi.heb:
*למני אשור.* 
אשר הוא ראש למרענו:
rashi.eng: *from Assyria.* which is the first of those who harmed us.

rashi.heb:
*וערי מצור.* 
כלומר ועד ערי מצור ויונתן תרגם ודמן חורמיני רבתא:
rashi.eng: *and the fortified cities.* I.e., and until the fortified cities. And Jonathan renders (as follows): the great dark mountains.

rashi.heb:
*וים מים.* 
והיושבים על ים האחרון אשר הוא במערב:
rashi.eng: *and the sea from the west.* And those dwelling near the Mediterranean Sea, which is in the west.

rashi.heb:
*והר ההר.* 
כמו ויושבי ההר ויונתן לא כן תרגם:
rashi.eng: *and the dwellers of the mountain.* Heb. וְהַר הָהָר, like יושְׁבֵי הָהָר. But Jonathan did not translate in that manner.

rashi.heb:
*יום לבנות גדריך.* 
הנביא מבשרו לישראל שיש יום כמוס ומוכן לבנות גדרות חרבותיהן:
rashi.eng: *[11] The day to build your walls.* The prophet informs Israel that there is a day preserved and prepared [for them] to build the walls of their ruins.

rashi.heb:
*יום ההוא ירחק.* 
ויבטל מעליכם חק גזירות הבבליים ופרסיים:
rashi.eng: *on that day the decree shall distance itself.* And the statute of the decrees of the nations shall be nullified from upon you.

rashi.heb:
*יום הוא ועדיך יבא.* 
בעידנא ההיא יתכנשון גלוותא דישראל דמן אתור וגו':
rashi.eng: *[12] It is a day, and shall come up to you.* At that time, the exiles of Israel shall be gathered in from Assyria.

notes.321: (tn, Heb): “on account of its inhabitants, because of the fruit of their deeds.”

rashi.heb:
*והיתה הארץ.* 
ארץ הבבליים ופרסיי':
rashi.eng: *And the land shall become.* The land of the nations.

notes.322: (tn): Or “with your scepter” (the Hebrew term can mean either “rod” or “scepter”).
notes.324: (tn): Or “in the midst of Carmel.” The Hebrew term translated “pastureland” may be a place name. The point seems to be that Israel is in a vulnerable position, like sheep in a thicket populated by predators, while rich pastureland (their homeland and God’s blessings) is in view.
notes.325: (sn): The regions of Bashan and Gilead, located in Transjordan, were noted for their rich grazing lands.
notes.326: (tn, Heb): “as in the days of antiquity.”

rashi.heb:
*שוכני לבדד.* 
שיהא שוכן בטח בדד:
rashi.eng: *who dwell alone.* That they should dwell alone, in security.

rashi.heb:
*יער בתוך כרמל.* 
ת"י דהוי צדין בחורשא יתיתבון ככרמלא אותן שהיו שוממים כיערות ישכנו לבדד בתוך כרמל שהוא מקום מיושב ויש לפרש:
rashi.eng: *a forest in the midst of a fruitful field.* Jonathan renders: Those who were desolate in a forest shall settle in the “karmel;” those who were desolate in the forests shall dwell alone in the midst of the “karmel,” which is a settled place. It is also possible to explain:

rashi.heb:
*שוכני לבדד.* 
ביערים לא יראו מחיות השדה כבתוך כרמל:
rashi.eng: *who dwell alone.* In the forests will not fear the wild beasts as [they would not] in the midst of a fruitful field.

notes.327: (tn, Heb): “him.” This probably refers to Israel in a collective sense. Because the switch from direct address to the third person is awkward, some prefer to emend the suffix to a second person form. In any case, it is necessary to employ a second person pronoun in the translation to maintain the connection for the English reader.
notes.328: (sn): I will show you miraculous deeds. In this verse the Lord responds to the petition of v. 14 with a brief promise of deliverance.

notes.330: (tn, Heb): “and their ears will be deaf.” Apparently this means the opposing nations will be left dumbfounded by the Lord’s power. Their inability to respond will make them appear to be deaf mutes.

notes.331: (tn, Heb): “like crawling things on the ground.” The parallelism suggests snakes are in view.
notes.332: (tn): �The�translation�assumes�that�the phrase אֶל־יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ (’el-y�hvah ’elohenu, “to the Lord our God”) goes with what precedes. Another option is to take the phrase with the following verb, in which case one could translate, “to the Lord our God they will turn in dread.”
notes.333: (tn, Heb): “they will be in dread and afraid.”
notes.334: (tn): The Lord is addressed directly using the second person.

rashi.heb:
*כזוחלי ארץ.* 
הם נחשים הזוחלי' על גחונם בעפר הארץ:
rashi.eng: *as those who crawl on the earth.* They are snakes, which crawl on their bellies on the dust of the earth.

rashi.heb:
*ירגזו ממסגרותיהם.* 
יחרדו מרוב דוחק איסוריהם ומסגר כלאם:
rashi.eng: *They shall quake from their imprisonment.* They shall quake because of the extreme narrowness of their imprisonment and the confinement of their captivity.

notes.335: (tn, Heb): “Who is a God like you?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “No one!”
notes.336: (tn, Heb): “one who.” The prayer moves from direct address (second person) in v. 18a to a descriptive (third person) style in vv. 18b-19a and then back to direct address (second person) in vv. 19b-20. Due to considerations of English style and the unfamiliarity of the modern reader with alternation of persons in Hebrew poetry, the entire section has been rendered as direct address (second person) in the translation.
notes.338: (tn, Heb): “of the remnant of his inheritance.”
notes.339: (tn, Heb): “he does not keep hold of his anger forever.”

notes.340: (tn): The verb יָשׁוּב (yashuv, “he will return”) is here used adverbially in relation to the following verb, indicating that the Lord will again show mercy.
notes.341: (tn): Some prefer to read יִכְבֹּס (yikhbos, “he will cleanse”; see HALOT 459 s.v. כבס pi). If the MT is taken as it stands, sin is personified as an enemy that the Lord subdues.
notes.342: (tn, Heb): “their sins,” but the final mem (ם) may be enclitic rather than a pronominal suffix. In this case the suffix from the preceding line (“our”) may be understood as doing double duty.
notes.343: (sn): In this metaphor the Lord disposes of Israel’s sins by throwing them into the waters of the sea (here symbolic of chaos).

notes.344: (tn): More literally, “You will extend loyalty to Jacob, and loyal love to Abraham.
notes.345: (tn, Heb): “our fathers.” The Hebrew term refers here to more distant ancestors, not immediate parents.
notes.346: (tn, Heb): “which you swore [or, “pledged”] to our fathers from days of old.”

rashi.heb:
*תתן אמת ליעקב.* 
ת"י תתיהב קושטיה דיעקב לבנוהי כמה דקיימתא ליה בבית אל טבות אברהם לזרעיה בתרוהי כמה דקיימתא ליה בין בתריא תדכר לנא עקידת יצחק תתן לנו באמת אשר הבטחת ליעקב האמת לנו דבריך אשר הבטחת ליעקב כי לא אעזבך (בראשית כט):
rashi.eng: *You shall give the truth of Jacob.* Jonathan paraphrases: You shall give the truth of Jacob to his sons, as You swore to him in Bethel; the loving-kindness of Abraham to his seed after him, as you swore to him ‘between the parts.’ You shall remember for us the binding of Isaac, etc. Give us the truth that You promised Jacob. Cause to come true Your word that You promised Jacob (Gen. 28:15): “For I will not forsake you.”

rashi.heb:
*חסד לאברהם.* 
שכר חסד אשר לאברהם אשר צוה לבניו לשמור דרך ה' לעשו' צדקה ומשפט ולכך לא נאמר וחסד אלא חסד האמת שתאמת לנו את הבטחת יעקב היא תהיה תשלום גמול חסדו של אברהם:
rashi.eng: *the loving-kindness of Abraham.* The reward for the loving-kindness of Abraham, [out of] which he commanded his sons to keep the way of the Lord: to perform righteousness and justice. Therefore, it does not say, “And the loving-kindness,” but “the loving-kindness.” The truth - that you will make come true the promise to Jacob - that will be the payment of the reward for Abraham’s loving-kindness.

rashi.heb:
*אשר נשבעת.* 
בעקידתו של יצחק בי נשבעתי נאם ה' יען אשר עשית וגומר:
rashi.eng: *which you swore.* at the binding of Isaac, (Gen 22:16) “I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that because you did this thing, etc.”
